//! Starter leftovers on the init-first path: `init --web` (or `--expo`) wrote
//! the todo starter, then the project replaced `snapback/schema.q`. The
//! starter's own files that still match the bytes init wrote, but no longer
//! fit the schema, are leftovers: `check` names them and `init --adapt`
//! removes or rewrites them. A file the project changed is never touched.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.2 — leftovers are judged by the starter's original bytes, never by name alone.
use super::starter::{self, Body, Platform};
use super::{OwnSchema, own_schema};
use std::path::Path;

/// One unmodified starter file that no longer fits the project's schema.
pub(crate) struct Leftover {
    pub path: &'static str,
    pub why: String,
    /// The text `init --adapt` writes; `None` removes the file.
    pub rewrite: Option<String>,
}

/// Starter operations its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
const STARTER_OPERATIONS: [&str; 4] = ["list", "add", "toggle", "remove"];

/// Whether a schema still has the starter's `todos` table and the operations
/// its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
pub(super) fn fits_todos(own: &OwnSchema) -> bool {
    own.tables.iter().any(|table| table == "todos")
        && STARTER_OPERATIONS.iter().all(|op| own.operations.iter().any(|name| name == op))
}

/// What the schema in `dir` leaves of the starter, and the advice that goes
/// with it (a sign-in the project must write by hand). No schema: nothing.
pub(crate) fn leftovers(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>) {
    let (found, advice, _) = plan(dir);
    (found, advice)
}

fn plan(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
    let Ok(Some(own)) = own_schema(dir) else { return (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new()) };
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut advice = Vec::new();
    let mut modified = Vec::new();
    let todos = fits_todos(&own);
    for (path, text) in starter::FIXTURES {
        let current = read(dir, path);
        if current.as_ref().is_some_and(|current| *current != super::without_design_references(text)) { modified.push(path.to_owned()); }
        if !todos && current.is_some_and(|current| current == super::without_design_references(text)) {
            let what = if path.ends_with("todos.jsonl") { "rows for the todo starter's `todos` table" } else { "cases for the todo starter's list/add/toggle/remove" };
            found.push(Leftover { path, why: format!("the unmodified {what}; your snapback/*.q has no todos table with those operations, so `snapback4 test` would refuse it"), rewrite: None });
        }
    }
    for platform in [Platform::Web, Platform::Expo] {
        if !screens(dir, platform, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut advice) {
            for path in [platform.paths().0, platform.paths().1] { if read(dir, path).is_some() { modified.push(path.to_owned()); } }
        }
    }
    if let Some(text) = read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts") {
        let wanted = starter::native_smoke(own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests));
        let recognized = if std::fs::symlink_metadata(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts")).is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink()) { None } else { super::proof_advice::native_template(&text) };
        if recognized.is_none() { modified.push("src/native-smoke.ts".to_owned()); }
        if recognized.is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir, &found) {
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why: "the unmodified helper is now supplied by snapback4-expo/native-smoke; the planned screens no longer import this copy".into(), rewrite: None });
        } else if text != wanted && let Some((version, password)) = recognized && smoke_referenced(dir, &found) {
            let old = text != starter::native_smoke(password);
            let why = if old {
                let mode = if password != own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests) { "; refresh also updates its sign-in mode" } else { "" };
                format!("an older starter version ({version}; adapt can refresh it){mode}")
            } else {
                "the unmodified native smoke helper uses a different starter sign-in mode (adapt can refresh it)".into()
            };
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
        }
    }
    if read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts").is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir, &found) && !found.iter().any(|f| f.path == "src/native-smoke.ts" && f.rewrite.is_none()) {
        advice.push("info: src/native-smoke.ts has no source reference; review it before a native smoke proof".into());
    }
    if !todos && let Some(web) = [false, true].into_iter().find(|web| super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, *web).is_some_and(|(_, template)| template.is_none())) {
        found.push(Leftover { path: "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", why: "the unmodified todo proof needs your screen's write assertions; keep a runnable frontend scaffold that explicitly reports the missing scenario".into(), rewrite: Some(super::proof::frontend_scaffold(web)) });
    }
    readme(dir, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut modified);
    app_json(dir, &mut found);
    expo_favicon(dir, &mut found);
    (found, advice, modified)
}

// A custom entry/component/proof can reference the helper too. Generated trees
// and dependency directories are not authored source; do not follow symlinks.
fn smoke_referenced(root: &Path, changes: &[Leftover]) -> bool {
    fn walk(root: &Path, dir: &Path, helper: &Path, changes: &[Leftover]) -> bool {
        let Ok(entries)=std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return true; };
        for entry in entries {
            let Ok(entry)=entry else {return true;};
            let Ok(kind)=entry.file_type() else {return true;};
            let path=entry.path();
            if kind.is_symlink() {
                if matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) {continue;}
                return true; // Unknown source may refer back to the local helper.
            }
            if kind.is_dir() {
                if !matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) && walk(root,&path,helper,changes) {return true;}
            } else if path!=helper && !path.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".d.ts")
                && path.extension().and_then(|e|e.to_str()).is_some_and(|e|matches!(e,"ts"|"tsx"|"js"|"jsx"|"mjs"|"cjs")) {
                let relative = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap().to_string_lossy();
                let text = if let Some(change) = changes.iter().find(|f| f.path == relative) {
                    let Some(text) = &change.rewrite else { continue; }; Some(text.clone())
                } else { std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok() };
                if text.is_none_or(|text| {
                    let text = text.replace("snapback4-expo/native-smoke", "");
                    if text.contains("/native-smoke") { return true; }
                    let compact: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
                    if ["from\"native-smoke\"", "from'native-smoke'", "import\"native-smoke\"", "import'native-smoke'"].iter().any(|s| compact.contains(*s)) { return true; }
                    // A CLI mode named native-smoke is not a module reference.
                    // Unknown dynamic imports/requires keep the local helper.
                    ["import(", "require("].iter().any(|call| compact.match_indices(*call).any(|(at, _)| {
                        let argument = &compact[at + call.len()..];
                        !argument.starts_with(['\'', '"']) || argument.starts_with("'native-smoke'") || argument.starts_with("\"native-smoke\"")
                    }))
                }) {return true;}
            }
        }
        false
    }
    walk(root,root,&root.join("src/native-smoke.ts"),changes)
}

/// The starter README, while it is still one init wrote (for either screen,
/// at the ports it names), when it describes another screen than the schema
/// now gets: the Todos README beside a project's schema, or the reverse.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (042): adapt rewrote the screen but left a README about todos and guest sign-in.
fn readme(dir: &Path, own: &OwnSchema, todos: bool, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>, modified: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let platform = if dir.join("src/App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Web } else if dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Expo } else { return };
    let title = super::title(dir);
    let personas = own.identity.is_none() && !own.personas.is_empty();
    let wanted_body = if todos { Body::Todos } else { Body::Home(None) };
    for path in ["README.md", "README.snapback.md"] {
        let Some(text) = read(dir, path) else { continue };
        let port = number_after(&text, "127.0.0.1:");
        let web_port = number_after(&text, "localhost:");
        let ports = [(port, web_port), (None, web_port), (port, None), (None, None)];
        // The offline paragraph names the schema's synced tables when init
        // wrote it; any of them (or 0.4.22's unconditional claim) still matches.
        let masked = starter::without_offline(&text);
        let explicit_online = platform == Platform::Web && read(dir, "src/client.ts").is_some_and(|client| client.contains("writes: \"online\""));
        let matched = ports.into_iter().find(|&(port, web_port)| {
            [(Body::Todos, false), (Body::Home(None), false), (Body::Home(None), true)].iter()
                .any(|(body, personas)| [false, true].iter().any(|password| [false, true].iter().any(|online| {
                    let readme = starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, body, *personas, &starter::Offline::Unknown, *password);
                    let readme = if *online { starter::online_readme(&readme) } else { readme };
                    masked == starter::without_offline(&super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&readme), port, web_port))
                })))
        });
        let Some((port, web_port)) = matched else { modified.push(path.to_owned()); continue };
        let wanted = super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, &wanted_body, personas, &own.offline, own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests))), port, web_port);
        let wanted = if explicit_online { starter::online_readme(&wanted) } else { wanted };
        let wanted = if todos { super::proof::readme(wanted) } else { wanted };
        if wanted == text { continue; }
        let about = if todos { "the todo starter's operations, which your snapback/*.q declares again" } else { "your snapback/*.q and the Home screen, named after this directory" };
        let only_proof = super::proof::without_readme(&wanted) == text;
        let only_offline = !text.starts_with("# Todos") && starter::without_offline(&wanted) == masked;
        // A schema that does not compile right now says nothing about what it syncs.
        if only_offline && !only_proof && own.offline == starter::Offline::Unknown { continue; }
        let why = if only_proof {
            "the unmodified starter README lacks frontend/day-two proof instructions; adapt adds them".to_owned()
        } else if only_offline {
            "the unmodified starter README says what works offline for another schema; adapt rewrites that paragraph from the tables your snapback/*.q syncs".to_owned()
        } else {
            format!("the unmodified starter README describes {}; adapt rewrites it to describe {about}", if text.starts_with("# Todos") { "the todo starter (its todos table and guest sign-in)" } else { "the Home screen for another schema" })
        };
        found.push(Leftover { path, why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
    }
}

/// An Expo `app.json` that still carries the todo starter's slug, scheme and
/// bundle ids (written by 0.4.21 and earlier): adapt names them after the
/// directory and changes nothing else in the file.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (067): adapted Expo apps kept dev.snapback4.todos.
fn app_json(dir: &Path, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>) {
    let Some(text) = read(dir, "app.json") else { return };
    let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { return };
    let expo = &config["expo"];
    let [(_, slug), (_, scheme), (_, bundle)] = starter::TODO_IDS;
    if expo["slug"] != slug || expo["scheme"] != scheme || expo["ios"]["bundleIdentifier"] != bundle || expo["android"]["package"] != bundle { return; }
    let (new_slug, new_scheme, new_bundle) = starter::app_ids(&super::title(dir));
    let quoted = |value: &str| format!("\"{value}\"");
    let rewrite = text.replace(&quoted(bundle), &quoted(&new_bundle)).replace(&quoted(slug), &quoted(&new_slug)).replace(&quoted(scheme), &quoted(&new_scheme));
    found.push(Leftover { path: "app.json", why: format!("the todo starter's ids (slug {slug}, scheme {scheme}, bundle id {bundle}); adapt names them after this directory ({new_slug}, {new_scheme}, {new_bundle})"), rewrite: Some(rewrite) });
}

// Repair only the exact SVG asset and setting emitted by 0.4.26. Custom
// images/settings remain owned by the app, including other SVG paths.
fn expo_favicon(dir: &Path, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>) {
    if read(dir, "assets/favicon.svg").as_deref() != Some(include_str!("starter/favicon.svg")) { return; }
    let Some(text) = read(dir, "app.json") else { return };
    let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { return };
    if config.pointer("/expo/web/favicon").and_then(|value| value.as_str()) != Some("./assets/favicon.svg") { return; }
    let why = "the unmodified Expo favicon is SVG, which Expo's web export requires to be raster".to_owned();
    if let Some(existing) = found.iter_mut().find(|change| change.path == "app.json") {
        let mut config: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(existing.rewrite.as_ref().unwrap()).unwrap();
        config["expo"]["web"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("favicon");
        existing.rewrite = Some(super::pretty(&config));
        existing.why.push_str("; Expo's web export also requires a raster favicon");
    } else {
        let mut config = config;
        config["expo"]["web"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("favicon");
        found.push(Leftover { path: "app.json", why: why.clone(), rewrite: Some(super::pretty(&config)) });
    }
    found.push(Leftover { path: "assets/favicon.svg", why, rewrite: None });
}

fn number_after(text: &str, prefix: &str) -> Option<u16> {
    let at = text.find(prefix)? + prefix.len();
    let digits: String = text[at..].chars().take_while(char::is_ascii_digit).collect();
    digits.parse().ok()
}

/// The sign-in a schema admits, as the starter screen it needs: the guest
/// screen (`None`), the persona picker (`Some(personas)`), or no starter
/// screen fits (`Err(advice)`).
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum SignIn { Guest, Password, Personas(Vec<String>) }
impl SignIn {
    fn label(&self) -> String {
        match self { Self::Guest => "the guest sign-in".into(), Self::Password => "the password sign-in".into(), Self::Personas(names) => format!("a persona picker ({})", names.join(", ")) }
    }
    fn personas(&self) -> Option<&[String]> { match self { Self::Personas(names) => Some(names), _ => None } }
}
fn wanted(own: &OwnSchema) -> Result<SignIn, &'static str> {
    match own.identity {
        Some((_, true)) => Ok(SignIn::Guest),
        Some((true, false)) => Ok(SignIn::Password),
        None if !own.personas.is_empty() => Ok(SignIn::Personas(own.personas.clone())),
        _ => Err("declares neither `use identity` nor `use personas`, so nobody can act: add `use identity` for the guest sign-in or `use personas alice, bob` for development, then rerun `snapback4 init --adapt`"),
    }
}

fn screens(dir: &Path, platform: Platform, own: &OwnSchema, todos: bool, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>, advice: &mut Vec<String>) -> bool {
    let (app_path, client_path) = platform.paths();
    let (Some(app), Some(client)) = (read(dir, app_path), read(dir, client_path)) else { return true };
    // Which starter screen is on disk, if both files are still as init wrote
    // them: its sign-in (guest, or a persona picker) and its body.
    let journal_shape = starter::Offline::Tables { synced: vec![], total: 0 };
    let explicit_online = platform == Platform::Web && client.contains("writes: \"online\"");
    let client_shape = normalized(&client);
    let matches_client = |reference: &str, personas: bool| [reference, starter::previous_client(platform, personas)].iter().any(|reference|
        client_shape == normalized(reference) || client_shape == normalized(&starter::web_client((*reference).to_owned(), &journal_shape)) || client_shape == normalized(&starter::online_web_client((*reference).to_owned())) || client_shape == normalized(&starter::expo_client((*reference).to_owned(), &journal_shape)));
    let current = [Body::Todos, Body::Home(first_read(&app))].into_iter().find_map(|body| [0, 1, 2, 3].into_iter().find_map(|version| {
        let screens = |personas: Option<&[String]>, password| match version { 1 => starter::previous_screens(platform, personas, &body, password), 2 => starter::wave14_screens(platform, personas, &body, password), 3 => starter::wave20_screens(platform, personas, &body, password), _ => starter::identity_screens(platform, personas, &body, password) };
        let (guest_app, guest_client) = screens(None, false);
        let (persona_app, persona_client) = screens(Some(&[]), false);
        let (password_app, password_client) = screens(None, true);
        if app == guest_app && matches_client(&guest_client, false) { Some((SignIn::Guest, body.clone())) }
        else if app == password_app && matches_client(&password_client, false) { Some((SignIn::Password, body.clone())) }
        else if app == persona_app && matches_client(&persona_client, true) { Some((SignIn::Personas(personas_of(&client)), body.clone())) }
        else { None }
    }));
    let Some((sign_in, body)) = current else { return false };
    // A Home keeps its read while the schema still declares that query
    // argument-free; a Home without one stays as written (it fits any schema).
    let wanted_body = match &body {
        _ if todos => Body::Todos,
        Body::Home(None) => Body::Home(None),
        Body::Home(Some(op)) if own.reads.contains(op) => body.clone(),
        _ => Body::Home(own.reads.first().cloned()),
    };
    // A sign-in no starter screen fits keeps the one on disk, with advice.
    let wanted_sign_in = match wanted(own) {
        Ok(wanted) => wanted,
        Err(why) => {
            advice.push(format!("{app_path} is the starter's {}, but your snapback/*.q {why}", sign_in.label()));
            sign_in.clone()
        }
    };
    let (app_text, mut client_text) = starter::identity_screens(platform, wanted_sign_in.personas(), &wanted_body, wanted_sign_in == SignIn::Password);
    client_text = if explicit_online { starter::online_web_client(client_text) } else if platform == Platform::Expo { starter::expo_client(client_text, &own.offline) } else { starter::web_client(client_text, &own.offline) };
    let client_changed = client_shape != normalized(&client_text);
    if wanted_sign_in == sign_in && app == app_text && wanted_body == body && !client_changed { return true; }
    let mut reasons = Vec::new();
    let mut client_leftover = None;
    if wanted_sign_in != sign_in {
        let (from, to) = (sign_in.label(), wanted_sign_in.label());
        let because = match &wanted_sign_in { SignIn::Personas(_) => "your snapback/*.q declares `use personas` and no `use identity`", SignIn::Password => "your snapback/*.q declares `use identity password`", SignIn::Guest => "your snapback/*.q admits guests" };
        reasons.push(format!("the unmodified starter screen shows {from}, but {because}; adapt writes {to}"));
        // Keep the backend port init wrote.
        if let Some(port) = port_of(&client) { client_text = client_text.replace("127.0.0.1:4400", &format!("127.0.0.1:{port}")); }
        client_leftover = Some(Leftover { path: client_path, why: format!("the unmodified starter client for {from}; adapt writes {to}"), rewrite: Some(client_text.clone()) });
    }
    if wanted_sign_in == sign_in && client_changed {
        if let Some(port) = port_of(&client) { client_text = client_text.replace("127.0.0.1:4400", &format!("127.0.0.1:{port}")); }
        let why = "the unmodified web client needs the device or principal journal selected by your schema's synced tables".to_owned();
        reasons.push(why.clone());
        client_leftover = Some(Leftover { path: client_path, why, rewrite: Some(client_text.clone()) });
    }
    if wanted_body != body {
        reasons.push(match (&wanted_body, &body) {
            (Body::Home(_), Body::Home(Some(op))) => format!("its Home screen reads api.{op}, which your snapback/*.q no longer declares as a query without required arguments; adapt writes the Home screen again{}", match &wanted_body { Body::Home(Some(next)) => format!(", reading api.{next}"), _ => String::new() }),
            (Body::Home(_), _) => "its Todos screen calls the starter's list/add/toggle/remove, which your snapback/*.q does not declare, so it would not typecheck; adapt writes a Home screen that compiles against any schema (the signed-in viewer, your operations from snapback/generated/api.ts, and your first query without required arguments rendered with matchRead) for you to replace".to_owned(),
            (Body::Todos, _) => "your snapback/*.q declares the todo starter's operations again; adapt writes the Todos screen back".to_owned(),
        });
    }
    let why = reasons.join("; ");
    let why = if why.starts_with("the unmodified") { why } else { format!("the unmodified starter screen: {why}") };
    found.push(Leftover { path: app_path, why, rewrite: Some(app_text) });
    found.extend(client_leftover);
    true
}

/// The `api` path a starter Home's first read calls, if it has one.
fn first_read(app: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let after = app.split_once("function FirstRead()")?.1;
    let op = after.split_once("useQuery(api.")?.1.split_once(',')?.0;
    Some(op.to_owned())
}

fn read(dir: &Path, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let path = dir.join(path);
    path.symlink_metadata().ok().filter(|metadata| metadata.is_file())?;
    std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()
}

/// A starter client without what init or the schema varies: the backend port
/// and the persona list.
fn normalized(client: &str) -> String {
    let lines = client.split_inclusive('\n').map(|line| {
        if line.starts_with(PERSONAS) { format!("{PERSONAS}[];\n") } else { line.to_owned() }
    }).collect::<String>();
    match port_of(&lines) { Some(port) => lines.replace(&format!("127.0.0.1:{port}"), "127.0.0.1:4400"), None => lines }
}

const PERSONAS: &str = "export const personas: readonly string[] = ";

fn personas_of(client: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    client.lines().find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix(PERSONAS))
        .and_then(|list| serde_json::from_str(list.trim_end().trim_end_matches(';')).ok()).unwrap_or_default()
}

fn port_of(client: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    let at = client.find("127.0.0.1:")? + "127.0.0.1:".len();
    let digits = client[at..].find(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(client.len() - at);
    (digits > 0).then(|| &client[at..at + digits])
}

/// One `check` line, or none: the leftovers and the command that fixes them.
pub(crate) fn report(dir: &Path) -> Option<String> {
    let (found, mut advice) = leftovers(dir);
    advice.extend(super::proof_advice::report(dir));
    if found.is_empty() && advice.is_empty() { return None; }
    if found.is_empty() { return Some(advice.join("\n")); }
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    for leftover in &found { lines.push(format!("  {}: {}", leftover.path, leftover.why)); }
    for line in &advice { lines.push(format!("  {line}")); }
    if !found.is_empty() {
        lines.push("  fix: snapback4 init --adapt (removes or rewrites only these files, which still match the starter; your own files are never touched)".into());
    }
    Some(format!("info: starter: {} from `snapback4 init` to review\n{}",
        if found.is_empty() { "a screen".to_owned() } else { format!("{} file{}", found.len(), if found.len() == 1 { "" } else { "s" }) },
        lines.join("\n")))
}

/// The same, for `check --json`: `null` when nothing is left over.
pub(crate) fn report_json(dir: &Path) -> serde_json::Value {
    let (found, mut advice) = leftovers(dir);
    advice.extend(super::proof_advice::report(dir));
    if found.is_empty() && advice.is_empty() { return serde_json::Value::Null; }
    serde_json::json!({
        "files": found.iter().map(|leftover| serde_json::json!({ "path": leftover.path, "why": leftover.why, "adapt": if leftover.rewrite.is_some() { "rewrite" } else { "remove" } })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "advice": advice,
        "fix": if found.is_empty() { serde_json::Value::Null } else { "snapback4 init --adapt".into() },
    })
}

/// `snapback4 init --adapt [dir]`.
pub(super) fn adapt(dir: &Path, dry_run: bool, apply: bool, day2: bool) -> i32 {
    let own = match own_schema(dir) {
        Ok(Some(own)) => own,
        Ok(None) => { eprintln!("init --adapt: no snapback/*.q in {}; nothing to adapt to (run `snapback4 init --web` or `--expo` first)", dir.display()); return 1; }
        Err(error) => { eprintln!("init: {error}"); return 2; }
    };
    let (found, mut advice, modified) = plan(dir);
    advice.extend(super::proof_advice::report(dir));
    let proof = match super::proof::plan(dir, &own, day2) {
        Ok(proof) => proof,
        Err(error) => { eprintln!("init --adapt proof: {error}"); return 2; }
    };
    if !found.is_empty() || !proof.is_empty() {
        println!("init --adapt: planned changes (only unmodified starter files):");
        for change in &found { println!("  {} {} — {}", if change.rewrite.is_some() { "rewrite" } else { "remove" }, change.path, change.why); }
    }
    for line in super::proof_advice::legacy_differences(dir, &proof) { println!("init --adapt: {line}"); }
    for (path, body) in &proof {
        if path.starts_with("versions/") {
            println!("  add {path} — capture current snapback/*.q and contemporary fixtures; legacy flat sources stay unchanged");
            continue;
        }
        let exists = dir.join(path).exists();
        println!("  {} {} — {} proof infrastructure", if *path == "package.json" { "extend" } else if exists { "replace" } else { "add" }, path, if exists { "inherited" } else { "missing" });
        if *path == "package.json" {
            let old: serde_json::Value = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join(path)).ok().and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str(&text).ok()).unwrap_or_default();
            let new: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(body).unwrap();
            for group in ["scripts", "devDependencies"] {
                let keys = old[group].as_object().into_iter().flat_map(|o|o.keys()).chain(new[group].as_object().into_iter().flat_map(|o|o.keys())).collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>();
                for key in keys { if old[group][key] != new[group][key] { println!("    {group}.{key}: {} → {}", old[group][key], new[group][key]); } }
            }
            if old.pointer("/snapback4/starter/day2") != new.pointer("/snapback4/starter/day2") {
                println!("    snapback4.starter.day2: {} → {}", old["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"], new["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"]);
            }
            println!("    serialize package.json (including script key ordering)");
        }
    }
    if !modified.is_empty() { println!("init --adapt: application-owned or modified files stay unchanged: {}", modified.join(", ")); }
    if dry_run || !apply {
        for line in advice { println!("init --adapt: {line}"); }
        if !fits_todos(&own) && [false,true].into_iter().any(|web| super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, web).is_some_and(|(_,template)|template.is_none())) { println!("init --adapt: no write scenario: add an app-specific frontend proof with snapback4/proof after replacing Home"); }
        println!("init --adapt: preview only; no files changed. Apply with:");
        println!("snapback4 init{} --adapt{} --apply", if dir == Path::new(".") { String::new() } else { format!(" '{}'", dir.to_string_lossy().replace('\'', "'\"'\"'")) }, if day2 { " --day2" } else { "" });
        return 0;
    }
    if let Err(error) = super::proof::apply(dir, &proof) { eprintln!("init --adapt proof: {error}"); return 2; }
    let mut removed = Vec::new();
    let mut rewritten = Vec::new();
    for leftover in &found {
        let path = dir.join(leftover.path);
        let result = match &leftover.rewrite {
            Some(text) => super::replace_file(&path, text).map(|()| rewritten.push(leftover.path)),
            None => std::fs::remove_file(&path).map(|()| removed.push(leftover.path)),
        };
        if let Err(error) = result { eprintln!("init --adapt: {}: {error}", path.display()); return 2; }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — adapt removes the files it names, never a directory: the next step writes fixtures/<table>.jsonl.
    if found.is_empty() && proof.is_empty() { println!("init --adapt: nothing to adapt — no unmodified starter file conflicts with your snapback/*.q"); }
    if !removed.is_empty() {
        let kept = if removed.iter().any(|path| path.starts_with("fixtures/")) { "; fixtures/ stays for your own rows" } else { "" };
        println!("init --adapt: removed {} (unmodified starter files{kept}; write your own as fixtures/<table>.jsonl and fixtures/test.cases.jsonl, `snapback4 guide testing`)", removed.join(" and "));
    }
    if !rewritten.is_empty() {
        let why = found.iter().find(|leftover| leftover.rewrite.is_some()).map(|leftover| leftover.why.as_str()).unwrap_or_default();
        println!("init --adapt: rewrote {} — {why}", rewritten.join(" and "));
    }
    if found.iter().any(|leftover| leftover.rewrite.as_deref().is_some_and(|text| text.contains("function Home("))) {
        println!("init --adapt: next: `snapback4 check` writes snapback/generated/api.ts for the Home screen; replace Home with your own screens (`snapback4 guide client`)");
    }
    for line in advice { println!("init --adapt: {line}"); }
    0
}

#[test]
fn untouched_wave9_screens_still_adapt_and_edited_clients_stay_owned() {
    for platform in [Platform::Web, Platform::Expo] {
        for password in [false, true] {
            let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("sb4-w10-adapt-{}-{platform:?}-{password}", std::process::id()));
            std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("snapback")).unwrap(); std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).unwrap();
            let schema = include_str!("starter/schema.q").replace("use identity ", "use identity password ");
            std::fs::write(dir.join("snapback/schema.q"), schema).unwrap();
            let (app, client) = starter::previous_screens(platform, None, &Body::Todos, password);
            let (app_path, client_path) = platform.paths();
            std::fs::write(dir.join(app_path), &app).unwrap(); std::fs::write(dir.join(client_path), &client).unwrap();
            let (changes, _) = leftovers(&dir);
            assert!(changes.iter().any(|change| change.path == app_path), "{platform:?}, password={password}: previous screens recognized");
            std::fs::write(dir.join(client_path), format!("{client}\n// application-owned edit\n")).unwrap();
            let (changes, _) = leftovers(&dir);
            assert!(!changes.iter().any(|change| change.path == app_path || change.path == client_path), "edited pair stays owned");
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
        }
    }
}


#[test]
fn untouched_wave14_screens_and_smoke_still_adapt() {
    for platform in [Platform::Web, Platform::Expo] {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("sb4-w14-adapt-{}-{platform:?}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("snapback")).unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).unwrap();
        let schema = include_str!("starter/schema.q").replace("use identity ", "use identity password ");

    }
}

#[test]
fn old_native_smoke_distinguishes_starter_age_from_sign_in_changes() {
    for password in [false, true] {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("sb4-r2-{}-{password}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("snapback")).unwrap();
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).unwrap();
        let schema = include_str!("starter/schema.q");
        let schema = if password { schema.replace("use identity", "use identity password") } else { schema.into() };
        std::fs::write(dir.join("snapback/schema.q"), schema).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(dir.join("src/custom.ts"), "import './native-smoke';").unwrap();
        for source in [include_str!("starter/previous/native-smoke-0.4.9.ts"), include_str!("starter/previous/native-smoke-0.4.16.ts"), include_str!("starter/previous/wave14/native-smoke.ts")] {
            for helper_password in [false,true] {
                std::fs::write(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts"), starter::native_smoke_version(helper_password, source)).unwrap();
                if helper_password && source == include_str!("starter/previous/native-smoke-0.4.9.ts") {
                    assert!(!leftovers(&dir).0.iter().any(|f|f.path=="src/native-smoke.ts"),"unshipped identity variants are not starter-owned");
                    continue;
                }
                let text = report(&dir).unwrap();
                assert!(text.contains("an older starter version") && !text.contains("previous schema") && !text.contains("not fit your schema"), "{text}");
                assert_eq!(text.contains("refresh also updates its sign-in mode"),helper_password!=password,"{text}");
            }
        }
        std::fs::write(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts"), starter::native_smoke(password)).unwrap();
        assert!(!leftovers(&dir).0.iter().any(|f|f.path=="src/native-smoke.ts"));
        std::fs::write(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts"), starter::native_smoke(!password)).unwrap();
        let current=report(&dir).unwrap();
        assert!(current.contains("different starter sign-in mode") && !current.contains("older starter") && !current.contains("previous schema"),"{current}");
        std::fs::write(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts"), format!("{}\n// mine", starter::wave14_native_smoke(password))).unwrap();
        assert!(!leftovers(&dir).0.iter().any(|f| f.path == "src/native-smoke.ts"));
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
    }
}

//! Starter leftovers on the init-first path: `init --web` (or `--expo`) wrote
//! the todo starter, then the project replaced `snapback/schema.q`. The
//! starter's own files that still match the bytes init wrote, but no longer
//! fit the schema, are leftovers: `check` names them and `init --adapt`
//! removes or rewrites them. A file the project changed is never touched.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.2 — leftovers are judged by the starter's original bytes, never by name alone.
use super::starter::{self, Body, Platform};
use super::{OwnSchema, own_schema};
use std::path::Path;

/// One unmodified starter file that no longer fits the project's schema.
pub(crate) struct Leftover {
    pub path: &'static str,
    pub why: String,
    /// The text `init --adapt` writes; `None` removes the file.
    pub rewrite: Option<String>,
}

/// Starter operations its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
const STARTER_OPERATIONS: [&str; 4] = ["list", "add", "toggle", "remove"];

/// Whether a schema still has the starter's `todos` table and the operations
/// its fixtures, cases and `Todos` screen call.
pub(super) fn fits_todos(own: &OwnSchema) -> bool {
    own.tables.iter().any(|table| table == "todos")
        && STARTER_OPERATIONS.iter().all(|op| own.operations.iter().any(|name| name == op))
}

/// What the schema in `dir` leaves of the starter, and the advice that goes
/// with it (a sign-in the project must write by hand). No schema: nothing.
pub(crate) fn leftovers(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>) {
    let (found, advice, _) = plan(dir);
    (found, advice)
}

fn plan(dir: &Path) -> (Vec<Leftover>, Vec<String>, Vec<String>) {
    let Ok(Some(own)) = own_schema(dir) else { return (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new()) };
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut advice = Vec::new();
    let mut modified = Vec::new();
    let todos = fits_todos(&own);
    for (path, text) in starter::FIXTURES {
        let current = read(dir, path);
        if current.as_ref().is_some_and(|current| *current != super::without_design_references(text)) { modified.push(path.to_owned()); }
        if !todos && current.is_some_and(|current| current == super::without_design_references(text)) {
            let what = if path.ends_with("todos.jsonl") { "rows for the todo starter's `todos` table" } else { "cases for the todo starter's list/add/toggle/remove" };
            found.push(Leftover { path, why: format!("the unmodified {what}; your snapback/*.q has no todos table with those operations, so `snapback4 test` would refuse it"), rewrite: None });
        }
    }
    for platform in [Platform::Web, Platform::Expo] {
        if !screens(dir, platform, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut advice) {
            for path in [platform.paths().0, platform.paths().1] { if read(dir, path).is_some() { modified.push(path.to_owned()); } }
        }
    }
    if let Some(text) = read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts") {
        let wanted = starter::native_smoke(own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests));
        let recognized = if std::fs::symlink_metadata(dir.join("src/native-smoke.ts")).is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink()) { None } else { super::proof_advice::native_template(&text) };
        if recognized.is_none() { modified.push("src/native-smoke.ts".to_owned()); }
        if recognized.is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir, &found) {
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why: "the unmodified helper is now supplied by snapback4-expo/native-smoke; the planned screens no longer import this copy".into(), rewrite: None });
        } else if text != wanted && let Some((version, password)) = recognized && smoke_referenced(dir, &found) {
            let old = text != starter::native_smoke(password);
            let why = if old {
                let mode = if password != own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests) { "; refresh also updates its sign-in mode" } else { "" };
                format!("an older starter version ({version}; adapt can refresh it){mode}")
            } else {
                "the unmodified native smoke helper uses a different starter sign-in mode (adapt can refresh it)".into()
            };
            found.push(Leftover { path: "src/native-smoke.ts", why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
        }
    }
    if read(dir, "src/native-smoke.ts").is_some() && !smoke_referenced(dir, &found) && !found.iter().any(|f| f.path == "src/native-smoke.ts" && f.rewrite.is_none()) {
        advice.push("info: src/native-smoke.ts has no source reference; review it before a native smoke proof".into());
    }
    if !todos && let Some(web) = [false, true].into_iter().find(|web| super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, *web).is_some_and(|(_, template)| template.is_none())) {
        found.push(Leftover { path: "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", why: "the unmodified todo proof needs your screen's write assertions; keep a runnable frontend scaffold that explicitly reports the missing scenario".into(), rewrite: Some(super::proof::frontend_scaffold(web)) });
    }
    readme(dir, &own, todos, &mut found, &mut modified);
    app_json(dir, &mut found);
    expo_favicon(dir, &mut found);
    (found, advice, modified)
}

// A custom entry/component/proof can reference the helper too. Generated trees
// and dependency directories are not authored source; do not follow symlinks.
fn smoke_referenced(root: &Path, changes: &[Leftover]) -> bool {
    fn walk(root: &Path, dir: &Path, helper: &Path, changes: &[Leftover]) -> bool {
        let Ok(entries)=std::fs::read_dir(dir) else { return true; };
        for entry in entries {
            let Ok(entry)=entry else {return true;};
            let Ok(kind)=entry.file_type() else {return true;};
            let path=entry.path();
            if kind.is_symlink() {
                if matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) {continue;}
                return true; // Unknown source may refer back to the local helper.
            }
            if kind.is_dir() {
                if !matches!(entry.file_name().to_str(),Some("node_modules"|".git"|".snapback4"|".expo"|"target"|"dist"|"build"|"generated")) && walk(root,&path,helper,changes) {return true;}
            } else if path!=helper && !path.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".d.ts")
                && path.extension().and_then(|e|e.to_str()).is_some_and(|e|matches!(e,"ts"|"tsx"|"js"|"jsx"|"mjs"|"cjs")) {
                let relative = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap().to_string_lossy();
                let text = if let Some(change) = changes.iter().find(|f| f.path == relative) {
                    let Some(text) = &change.rewrite else { continue; }; Some(text.clone())
                } else { std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok() };
                if text.is_none_or(|text| {
                    let text = text.replace("snapback4-expo/native-smoke", "");
                    if text.contains("/native-smoke") { return true; }
                    let compact: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
                    if ["from\"native-smoke\"", "from'native-smoke'", "import\"native-smoke\"", "import'native-smoke'"].iter().any(|s| compact.contains(*s)) { return true; }
                    // A CLI mode named native-smoke is not a module reference.
                    // Unknown dynamic imports/requires keep the local helper.
                    ["import(", "require("].iter().any(|call| compact.match_indices(*call).any(|(at, _)| {
                        let argument = &compact[at + call.len()..];
                        !argument.starts_with(['\'', '"']) || argument.starts_with("'native-smoke'") || argument.starts_with("\"native-smoke\"")
                    }))
                }) {return true;}
            }
        }
        false
    }
    walk(root,root,&root.join("src/native-smoke.ts"),changes)
}

/// The starter README, while it is still one init wrote (for either screen,
/// at the ports it names), when it describes another screen than the schema
/// now gets: the Todos README beside a project's schema, or the reverse.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (042): adapt rewrote the screen but left a README about todos and guest sign-in.
fn readme(dir: &Path, own: &OwnSchema, todos: bool, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>, modified: &mut Vec<String>) {
    let platform = if dir.join("src/App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Web } else if dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() { Platform::Expo } else { return };
    let title = super::title(dir);
    let personas = own.identity.is_none() && !own.personas.is_empty();
    let wanted_body = if todos { Body::Todos } else { Body::Home(None) };
    for path in ["README.md", "README.snapback.md"] {
        let Some(text) = read(dir, path) else { continue };
        let port = number_after(&text, "127.0.0.1:");
        let web_port = number_after(&text, "localhost:");
        let ports = [(port, web_port), (None, web_port), (port, None), (None, None)];
        // The offline paragraph names the schema's synced tables when init
        // wrote it; any of them (or 0.4.22's unconditional claim) still matches.
        let masked = starter::without_offline(&text);
        let explicit_online = platform == Platform::Web && read(dir, "src/client.ts").is_some_and(|client| client.contains("writes: \"online\""));
        let matched = ports.into_iter().find(|&(port, web_port)| {
            [(Body::Todos, false), (Body::Home(None), false), (Body::Home(None), true)].iter()
                .any(|(body, personas)| [false, true].iter().any(|password| [false, true].iter().any(|online| {
                    let readme = starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, body, *personas, &starter::Offline::Unknown, *password);
                    let readme = if *online { starter::online_readme(&readme) } else { readme };
                    masked == starter::without_offline(&super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&readme), port, web_port))
                })))
        });
        let Some((port, web_port)) = matched else { modified.push(path.to_owned()); continue };
        let wanted = super::localize(path, &super::without_design_references(&starter::identity_readme(platform, &title, &wanted_body, personas, &own.offline, own.identity.is_some_and(|(password, guests)| password && !guests))), port, web_port);
        let wanted = if explicit_online { starter::online_readme(&wanted) } else { wanted };
        let wanted = if todos { super::proof::readme(wanted) } else { wanted };
        if wanted == text { continue; }
        let about = if todos { "the todo starter's operations, which your snapback/*.q declares again" } else { "your snapback/*.q and the Home screen, named after this directory" };
        let only_proof = super::proof::without_readme(&wanted) == text;
        let only_offline = !text.starts_with("# Todos") && starter::without_offline(&wanted) == masked;
        // A schema that does not compile right now says nothing about what it syncs.
        if only_offline && !only_proof && own.offline == starter::Offline::Unknown { continue; }
        let why = if only_proof {
            "the unmodified starter README lacks frontend/day-two proof instructions; adapt adds them".to_owned()
        } else if only_offline {
            "the unmodified starter README says what works offline for another schema; adapt rewrites that paragraph from the tables your snapback/*.q syncs".to_owned()
        } else {
            format!("the unmodified starter README describes {}; adapt rewrites it to describe {about}", if text.starts_with("# Todos") { "the todo starter (its todos table and guest sign-in)" } else { "the Home screen for another schema" })
        };
        found.push(Leftover { path, why, rewrite: Some(wanted) });
    }
}

/// An Expo `app.json` that still carries the todo starter's slug, scheme and
/// bundle ids (written by 0.4.21 and earlier): adapt names them after the
/// directory and changes nothing else in the file.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#7.4 — wave 6 (067): adapted Expo apps kept dev.snapback4.todos.
fn app_json(dir: &Path, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>) {
    let Some(text) = read(dir, "app.json") else { return };
    let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { return };
    let expo = &config["expo"];
    let [(_, slug), (_, scheme), (_, bundle)] = starter::TODO_IDS;
    if expo["slug"] != slug || expo["scheme"] != scheme || expo["ios"]["bundleIdentifier"] != bundle || expo["android"]["package"] != bundle { return; }
    let (new_slug, new_scheme, new_bundle) = starter::app_ids(&super::title(dir));
    let quoted = |value: &str| format!("\"{value}\"");
    let rewrite = text.replace(&quoted(bundle), &quoted(&new_bundle)).replace(&quoted(slug), &quoted(&new_slug)).replace(&quoted(scheme), &quoted(&new_scheme));
    found.push(Leftover { path: "app.json", why: format!("the todo starter's ids (slug {slug}, scheme {scheme}, bundle id {bundle}); adapt names them after this directory ({new_slug}, {new_scheme}, {new_bundle})"), rewrite: Some(rewrite) });
}

// Repair only the exact SVG asset and setting emitted by 0.4.26. Custom
// images/settings remain owned by the app, including other SVG paths.
fn expo_favicon(dir: &Path, found: &mut Vec<Leftover>) {
    if read(dir, "assets/favicon.svg").as_deref() != Some(include_str!("starter/favicon.svg")) { return; }
    let Some(text) = read(dir, "app.json") else { return };
    let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { return };
    if config.pointer("/expo/web/favicon").and_then(|value| value.as_str()) != Some("./assets/favicon.svg") { return; }
    let why = "the unmodified Expo favicon is SVG, which Expo's web export requires to be raster".to_owned();
    if let Some(existing) = found.iter_mut().find(|change| change.path == "app.json") {
        let mut config: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(existing.rewrite.as_ref().unwrap()).unwrap();
        config["expo"]["web"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("favicon");
        existing.rewrite = Some(super::pretty(&config));
        existing.why.push_str("; Expo's web export also requires a raster favicon");
    } else {
        let mut config = config;
        config["expo"]["web"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("favicon");
        found.push(Leftover { path: "app.json", why: why.clone(), rewrite: Some(super::pretty(&config)) });
    }
    found.push(Leftover { path: "assets/favicon.svg", why, rewrite: None });
}

fn number_after(text: &str, prefix: &str) -> Option<u16> {
    let at = text.find(prefix)? + prefix.len();
    let digits: String = text[at..].chars().take_while(char::is_ascii_digit).collect();
    digits.parse().ok()
}

/// The sign-in a schema admits, as the starter screen it needs: the guest
/// screen (`None`), the persona picker (`Some(personas)`), or no starter
/// screen fits (`Err(advice)`).
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum SignIn { Guest, Password, Personas(Vec<String>) }
impl SignIn {
    fn label(&self) -> String {
        match self { Self::Guest => "the guest sign-in".into(), Self::Password => "the password sign-in".into(), Self::Personas(names) => format!("a persona picker ({})", names.join(", ")) }
    }
    fn personas(&self) -> Option<&[String]> { match self { Self::Personas(names) => Some(names), _ => None } }
}
fn wanted(own: &OwnSchema) -> Result<SignIn, &'static str> {
    match own.identity {
        Some((_, true)) => Ok(SignIn::Guest),
        Some((true, false)) => Ok(SignIn::Password),
        None if !own.personas.is_empty() => Ok(SignIn::Personas(own.personas.clone())),
        _ => Err("declares neither `use identity` nor `use personas`, so nobody can act: add `use identity` for the guest sign-in or `use personas alice, bob` for development, then rerun `snapback4 init --adapt`"),
    }
}

    // them: its sign-in (guest, or a persona picker) and its body.
    let journal_shape = starter::Offline::Tables { synced: vec![], total: 0 };
    let explicit_online = platform == Platform::Web && client.contains("writes: \"online\"");

async function clickSvg(page, control) {

  await page.mouse.click(box.x + box.width / 2, box.y + box.height / 2);
}

# Staging with real users

Staging runs real password users and application rules under serve. Use it for shared previews and probe:serve, with roles provisioned by a local operator.

```quarry
use identity password
table roles:
  principal: principal
  role: enum('admin', 'member')
  unique principal
  immutable principal
  read <- .principal = viewer or viewer = 'service:operator'
  insert <- viewer = 'service:operator'
  update <- viewer = 'service:operator'
  online only
mutation provision(principal: principal, role: enum('admin', 'member')):
  require viewer = 'service:operator' else NOT_OPERATOR
  return upsert roles[principal] { principal, role }
query myRole():
  return roles[viewer]
table notes:
  owner: principal
  body: text 1..200
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  online only
mutation add(body: text 1..200):
  return insert notes { owner: viewer, body }
query myNotes(c: cursor ?):
  return notes where .owner = viewer first 20 by .id after c
```

Use `serve` for staging, shared previews and `probe:serve`. It enforces the same
password identity and rules as production. `dev` always advertises
`development:true` in `/auth/config`, even with closed doors; probes should
refuse it. `guide deploy` covers release evolution; PROD2 owns starter adaptation.

## Password roles and operator provisioning

Save this complete source as `snapback/schema.q` in an app with snapback4 installed.
Signup creates an account without a role. Only the local filesystem operator can
bootstrap this roster. The insert rule enforces the boundary independently of
the mutation. SEC owns self-promotion diagnostics and invariant proofs.

## Stand up staging

Run `npx snapback4 check` to generate the API. Save this as `staging.mjs` next to
snapback/, then run `node staging.mjs`. Use `node staging.mjs --once` for CI setup
and shutdown. The deployment and private credentials file remain for inspection;
choose fresh names for each independent run. Add both to .gitignore. PORT_LO and
PORT_HI optionally choose a port range. The printed URL belongs to `serve`.

```js
import { openSync, writeFileSync, closeSync } from "node:fs";
import { deploy, startServe } from "snapback4/proof";
import { api } from "./snapback/generated/api.ts";

await deploy("staging", "snapback", { args: ["--staging"] });
const host = await startServe("staging", { seedUsers: {
  roles: { admin: 2, member: 2 }, provision: api.provision,
} });
try {
  // This file contains real passwords and bearer tokens. Never commit it.
  const fd = openSync("staging-users.json", "wx", 0o600);
  try { writeFileSync(fd, JSON.stringify(host.sessions)); } finally { closeSync(fd); }
  for (const accounts of Object.values(host.sessions)) {
    for (const account of accounts) {
      const response = await fetch(host.url + "/m/add", {
        method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${account.token}` },
        body: JSON.stringify({ args: { body: `Welcome ${account.role}` } }),
        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000),
      });
      if ((await response.json()).state !== "sent") throw Error("staging data write refused");
    }
  }
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ backendUrl: host.url, credentialsFile: "staging-users.json" }));
  if (!process.argv.includes("--once")) await new Promise(resolve => {
    process.once("SIGTERM", resolve); process.once("SIGINT", resolve);
  });
} finally { await host.stop(); }
```

`host.seedAccounts({roles, provision, args?})` performs additional batches; an
optional `args(account)` merges over `{principal, role}` (explicit keys win).
Use `service: "ops"` for a provisioning mutation authorized as `service:ops`.
Each call creates new random email/password pairs and returns role arrays of
`{role,email,password,principal,token,expiresAt}`. Ordinary sessions last seven
days; sign in again with `login` from snapback4/auth when needed. Setup is
sequential and bounded (default five minutes, timeoutMs overrides it, max 100
accounts). Identity 429 refusals wait for retryAfterMs (Retry-After on older
servers), at most four attempts per account within the remaining setup budget.
SDK guest/signup/login share this policy (timeoutMs defaults to three minutes;
signal cancels a request or wait). Ambiguous writes never retry. Partial failure can leave accounts/grants: inspect or discard this
disposable deployment before retrying. Returned credentials never enter helper
logs. Print them only to a private operator destination, as above.

## Production refuses bulk setup

`deploy --staging` can classify only a new store. Existing unmarked stores are
production, and refuse relabelling. Classification stays with the store across
hot deploys, rollbacks and restarts; copying production into a directory named
staging does not change it. `deploy --check --staging` does not mark a store.
There is no promotion flag: deploy real production into its own fresh directory
and provision only intended users. `seedAccounts` and startServe's seedUsers
refuse production or dev before minting a token or creating any account. A
normal production startServe still supports operatorToken for explicit grants.

### E_STAGING

E_STAGING refuses production relabelling or bulk account setup on a non-staging
host. Choose a separate fresh `deploy --staging` store; use the explicit
first-admin recipe below for intended production users. Source edits and a
directory named staging never change a production store's classification.


### Account setup refusals

E_STAGING_INPUT means the account plan is invalid. Provide 1..100 accounts,
named roles, a declared mutation handle and a positive timeoutMs before setup.

E_STAGING_TIMEOUT means the setup deadline expired. Partial accounts/grants
may exist; inspect or discard the disposable deployment before retrying.

E_STAGING_SIGNUP means password signup refused or returned an invalid session.
Inspect the underlying refusal; partial accounts/grants may exist, so inspect
or discard the disposable deployment before retrying.

E_STAGING_PROVISION means the operator mutation refused or returned an invalid
reply. Repair its arguments and operator-only rules; partial accounts/grants
may exist, so inspect or discard the disposable deployment before retrying.

### Identity request deadline

E_IDENTITY_TIMEOUT is the internal sign-in deadline cause (SDK E_OFFLINE).
Signup outcome may be unknown: inspect before retrying. Increase timeoutMs to
allow server retryAfterMs waits. seedAccounts maps it to E_STAGING_TIMEOUT
with the partial-account recovery guidance above.

## First admin on production

Deploy the same schema with `npx snapback4 deploy production` (omit --staging).
Save the following as `first-admin.mjs`. Set FIRST_ADMIN_EMAIL and
FIRST_ADMIN_PASSWORD privately, then run `node first-admin.mjs` as the store
owner while no other serve owns its port. This script starts and stops serve;
restart it normally afterwards. For an already running deployment use
`snapback4 token --service operator --days 1 --release production` locally and
the same authenticated mutation. Keep the service token out of the frontend.

```js
import { signup, login } from "snapback4/auth";
import { startServe } from "snapback4/proof";
const email = process.env.FIRST_ADMIN_EMAIL, password = process.env.FIRST_ADMIN_PASSWORD;
if (!email || !password) throw Error("Set FIRST_ADMIN_EMAIL and FIRST_ADMIN_PASSWORD privately");
const host = await startServe("production");
try {
  // Login first so rerunning this script preserves the existing account and grant.
  let account = await login(host.url, email, password);
  if (!account.ok) account = await signup(host.url, email, password);
  if (!account.ok) throw Error(account.why.message);
  const token = await host.operatorToken();
  const response = await fetch(host.url + "/m/provision", {
    method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({ args: { principal: account.session.principal, role: "admin" } }),
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000),
  });
  if ((await response.json()).state !== "sent") throw Error("operator grant refused");
  console.log("First admin provisioned; sign in with the chosen email and password");
} finally { await host.stop(); }
```

Reruns authenticate the same email/password and upsert the same roster row.
A wrong password refuses without changing an existing grant. No first-user race or self-promotion mutation is needed. Subsequent grants use
the same operator process or an explicitly authorized admin policy. Invite codes
must be server-validated, single-use grants issued by an authorized operator;
an arbitrary caller-supplied code or role is not authority.

## Local fixture tools are explicit

Password-only dev closes /seed, /dev/* and persona headers by default.
`dev --unsafe-dev-doors` explicitly opens local fixture and clock tools and
prints a warning; it still requires loopback Host/Origin, and personas must be
declared with `use personas`. The local token-mint protocol keeps its existing
private store-owner proof. Serve never opens these development tools.
`/auth/config` reports `environment`, `development`, and `devDoors` separately.
`startDev()` persists by default, matching native dev; pass args:["--memory"]
for disposable storage. now() needs the explicit clock door on password-only
dev. A proof for real users uses the serve recipe above.

## Time and reused stores

`await host.advance("49h")` returns `{now, fired, held}`; `await host.now()` still
returns a timestamp. The CLI `clock advance 49h --release staging` returns the
same outcomes. Fired means enqueued, so inspect each run state for parked work.
Every held schedule gives a reason and next boundary. Saved boundaries survive
restart: each boundary fires once; missed periods coalesce unless eachBoundary
is explicit. A reused store can hold a due application row because that window
already ran. The helper and CLI print the saved-boundary hold and recovery on
stderr. Advance beyond the saved boundary's next window, keep --clock-offset
across serve restarts when continuing, or deploy a fresh staging directory for
an independent test. Never replay a lost advance reply. Time travel also ages
sessions and unplaced uploads: log in again and upload bytes after a large jump.

# Client and operations

[Back to the package guide](./README.md).

For TypeScript actions use the generated `server()` wrapper described in
[server handlers](./SERVER.md); it enforces the application's precise handler
signatures. A custom runtime host can use the lower-level registry entry below
with that generated manifest and already checked handlers. It does not infer
application-specific argument/result types itself:

```ts
import { startServer, type ServerHandlers } from "snapback4/server";
import { manifest } from "../snapback/generated/server";

function hostCheckedHandlers(handlers: ServerHandlers, signal: AbortSignal) {
  return startServer(manifest, handlers, { signal });
}
```

## Offline web starter

`npx snapback4 init --web` writes a one-screen Vite + React todos app on
`createApp` with `webDevice()`; `npx snapback4 init --web --template chat`
copies the maintained Vite chat reference, including its production app shell,
account-bound saved route and write IDs. Default `init` remains schema-only.
Run `npm install`, `npx snapback4 check`, then
`npx snapback4 dev` and `npm run dev` in separate terminals. Build with
`VITE_SNAPBACK_URL=https://your-backend npm run build`; serve `dist/` over HTTPS.
The chat's routes use `#room=<id>`.

The build ends with `snapback4 web-shell dist`. Navigations use the active
worker's cached HTML even online, so its HTML and lazy assets stay together
until a waiting build activates after the old tabs close. This command also works on
`expo export -p web` output: it precaches every file in a content-hashed cache,
registers `snapback4-sw.js` in every HTML file idempotently, and resolves exported
subpages (`/contact` and `/contact/` to `contact.html`, then `/about/` to
`about/index.html` when `about.html` is absent) online and offline before falling
back to the root `index.html`. Pass `--base /chat/` when serving a subpath;
use the same base in the bundler. For Vite run
`npx vite build --base=/chat/ && npx snapback4 web-shell dist --base /chat/`.
It waits for old tabs to close before switching builds. Development has no worker.
Keep all exported files nonpersonalized; this is a static export, not SSR.
Cross-origin requests and non-exported API/media requests pass through untouched.
The worker never caches network navigation responses. The starter explicitly uses
`localStorageSessionStore()` for page-restart continuity; any script on that
origin can read the token. Choose this persistence deliberately.

Held room navigation reads conversation and membership before rendering the
thread; unknown offline rooms remain uncertain. Write references are saved
before SDK dispatch and reopened with `usePendingWrite(op, id)`, without
resubmission. `markRead` demonstrates a nonpredicting queued write. Failed and
unknown receipts stay visible; a settled write does not imply a fresh read.
Sign-out hides the account, completes only after local credentials are removed,
and keeps its replica/outbox intact. A storage failure stays visible for retry.
For a keyed text/media send, use the intent-card recipe below; keep saved failure references scoped to this account and backend.
See the generated README for residency tables, horizon choices and the
production offline-reopen journey; fixture residency remains
`test --residency --fixture <directory> --as <principal>`.

For a browser proof, register the application's own app and generated API
(starters do this; the hook is active only under `?witness=web`):

```ts
import { registerWebWitness, witnessForm } from "snapback4/witness-web";
import { createApp } from "snapback4/app";
import { localStorageSessionStore } from "snapback4/auth";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
const app = createApp({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:4400", sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore() });
registerWebWitness(app, api);
export function submitMessage(event: Event, conversationId: string, body: string) {
  return witnessForm(app, event, async mutate => { await mutate(api.send, { conversationId, body }); });
}
```

`npm run build:web && snapback4 witness web dist` proves the first durable
mutation reaches `sent`; `--mutation NAME --args JSON` supplies application
values. Password accounts use `--email EMAIL --password-env ENV_VAR`, with
`--url URL` for an existing backend. See `guide testing` for lifecycle and
idempotence limits; add `--field Task --value "Browser proof" --button Add` for the starter's visible form. The observer arms before clicking and requires that write's sent receipt.

## 4. The client

**Constructor compatibility:** ready `Read<T>` values now require `existence`. Readers keep `isReady`/`isLoading`/`isDenied`; custom clients and mocks must classify their published value as `present`, `absent` or `partial`. No wire field was added. See `guide client` for the rules and point-read narrowing.

`createApp` is the ordinary entry point. Construct it once outside React render.

| Program | Constructor |
|---|---|
| Node script, seed, test or worker | `createClient({ url, persona })` from `snapback4/client` in development; `createClient({ url, session })` after `signup`/`login` from `snapback4/auth` |
| Browser app, no synced table | `createApp({ url, sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore() })` under `AppProvider`: writes are journaled without a device, no wasm (below) |
| Browser app with synced tables | `createApp({ url, device: webDevice(), sessionStore })` under `AppProvider`; the device is about 650 KB gzip of wasm (below) |
| Expo app | `createApp({ url, device: nativeAvailable() ? nativeDevice : undefined, sessionStore })`; `webDevice()` on web |

**Browser writes need `createApp`.** A bare `createClient()` in a browser has
no synchronous write journal and refuses every mutation with `E_ADMISSION`;
reads still work. `createApp` journals each click before `mutate` returns: a
write survives a reload or a same-turn navigation, and the server runs it at
most once. When no table declares `sync`, it does this without a device (see
"Browser writes without a device"); synced tables need `webDevice()`.

**Budget for the device before choosing it.** `webDevice()` is the
whole local interpreter compiled to wasm: about 2.1 MB raw, 650 KB gzip (a
release budget caps the gzip size), plus a 24 KB worker, on top of the app's
JavaScript. A Vite production build emits it as its own asset, and the
device fetches it when it opens at restore or sign-in. It buys offline reads
and predictions over synced tables. With no synced table, omit it: the same
writing page measured 274,853 B raw (88,485 B gzip) of JavaScript and no wasm,
against 2,503,672 B (766,377 B gzip) with `webDevice()` (Vite production
builds of one page). A browser page that never writes
needs neither: every client reads, and `readOnly: true` silences the write
warning (`guide read-only`). An Expo app pays nothing on phones (the native
module, or Expo Go's online tier) and the same wasm on Expo web.

Its auth is `restoring` while opening or clearing a session, then becomes `signed-out` or `signed-in` with `viewer`.
`ready` resolves after restoration; `auth.onChange` observes it. Signup, login and
guest return `SignIn`; refusals are `{ ok: false, why }`. Logout clears local
credentials and attempts server revocation; `logoutEverywhere` revokes every
session after server confirmation. `auth.why` exposes a restore/storage failure.

```tsx
import { createApp } from "snapback4/app";
import { localStorageSessionStore } from "snapback4/auth";
import { webDevice } from "snapback4/web";
import { AppProvider, useAuth, useRelease } from "snapback4/react";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
const app = createApp({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:4400", device: webDevice(), sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore(),
  assets: { keep: "viewed", maxBytes: 67108864 },
});
function Account() {
  const auth = useAuth(), release = useRelease();
  return <button data-release={"generation" in release ? release.generation : "unavailable"} onClick={() => void (auth.state === "signed-in" ? auth.logout() : auth.guest())}>{auth.state}</button>;
}
function Root() { return AppProvider({ app, children: <Account /> }); }
async function send(conversationId: string) {
  await app.ready;
  return app.mutate(api.send, { conversationId, body: "Hello" });
}
```

Omit `device` for the online tier; pass `nativeDevice` or `processDevice()` for
other local hosts. `fetch` injects the transport. Device-less identity apps require
`sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore()` in browsers; this requirement is also
checked by TypeScript. A custom store must provide the browser journal authority.
Device hosts may omit the store for memory-only sessions. Web persistence is explicit. `app.client` changes on restore, sign-in, logout and account switch;
`AppProvider` supplies that client to all existing hooks and resets account-owned
component state. `useAuth()` returns the current state, viewer, failure and actions.
Call `app.close()` to stop a runtime while preserving its session for restart;
close finishes local work without waiting for a held network response. A known
rotation successor is saved; a later unkept successor is retired.
Its previously exposed client is revoked immediately. Already-started session
persistence finishes during cleanup; an unread rotation cannot delay close.
Close also ends queued auth network waits; background revocation still owns late acknowledgements.
`AppOptions` inherits the local client's application configuration. `assets` and
`waitSeconds` pass through on every local open, including restore and account
switch; both are ignored when `device` is omitted. `waitSeconds` sets the change
feed's long-poll duration (default 25 seconds). `assets` controls ordinary viewed
media retention as described below. Its `maxBytes` must be a nonnegative safe
integer. Invalid local asset configuration reports `E_CLIENT` at `app.assets`
through `ready`, sign-in results and `auth.why` before any session or network
work; correct the options and create the app again. Kept credentials remain intact.
Identity and sessions remain owned by
`app.auth` and its `sessionStore`; `persona`, `session` and `guest` are lower-level
client options, not app configuration.
`app.auth.logout()` signs this user out of the shared session storage. It
fences restoration and same-principal sign-ins already in flight, commits a
logout tombstone without waiting for network requests, and retires every
same-principal credential in that custody in the background: peer rotations,
pending successors and newer deliberate logins, whatever their epoch. A stale
Bob facade cannot delete or revoke Alice's later login. This rule is shared by
full and read-only apps; their separate storage namespaces remain isolated.
When another app replaces the stored session during restoration, opening restarts
with that session. A stale restoration or rejected bearer cannot overwrite or
delete the other app's stored successor.
### App-owned online access

A device app uses `app.online` for a server snapshot, live server observation,
ephemeral signal or action. `useOnline()` returns that arm under `AppProvider`:

```tsx
import { useOnline } from "snapback4/react";
import { createApp } from "snapback4/app";
import { localStorageSessionStore } from "snapback4/auth";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
const app = createApp({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:4400", sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore() });
function TypingButton({ room }: { room: string }) {
  const online = useOnline();
  return <button onClick={() => void online.mutate(api.setTyping, { room })}>Typing</button>;
}
async function serverSnapshot() {
  const read = await app.online.query(api.inboxCards, {});
  return read; // Render with matchRead; guide social has a complete screen.
}
```

`online.query` returns the same settled Read as `client.query`; `online.observe`
uses the same observation/keep contract. These evaluate at the server without
waiting on replica acquisition or pending predictions. They do not merge local
predictions or promise unlimited completeness: server cuts, continuations and
refusals still apply. For Trending/Insights-style snapshots this avoids the
replica's bounded settlement attempt; ordinary device screens keep `useQuery`.
`TrendingSnapshot` in `guide social` renders every state with `matchRead` and
provides Refresh for another one-shot. Use `online.act` for actions (the device
client's existing `act` also goes to the server). Durable mutations belong to
`app.mutate`/`useMutation`, retaining the existing outbox and admission guarantees;
`online.mutate` accepts only generated ephemeral operations.

The `Online` type (`snapback4/app`) exposes `query`, `observe`, `mutate`, `act`,
`link`, `onLink`, `viewer`, `now` and `readOnly`. It exposes no bearer, Session,
asset headers, refresh, close or sign-out method, even at runtime. The app owns
retirement. Rotation replaces the arm; `useOnline` subscribes automatically,
and headless consumers can use `app.onOnlineChange`. Reacquire `app.online` after
a change; cached old handles refuse `E_AUTH`. Account change, sign-out and close
withdraw observations and fence new requests, including requests queued behind
an asynchronous authority check. In both device and no-device apps, each arm
operation retains its originating arm and credential fence through queues,
refresh waits and retries; the transport rechecks it after shared authority,
immediately before dispatch. It cannot borrow the replacement credential.
Observation and renewal sharing stays within an arm. An arm refusal does not
invalidate the app's current session. Dispatched signals/actions retain their outcome;
the private device arm drains for up to 30 seconds before closing. An action
whose response never arrives then returns pending with its original ID. It never logs out
the app. Cleanup during ordinary screen unmount can still send stopTyping;
cleanup after credential retirement cannot send, and the four-second typing
expiry covers it. The SDK fences immediately: it does not delay retirement for
a best-effort stop or send that stop as the next account.

While signed out, operations refuse `E_AUTH`. When disconnected, one-shots,
signals and actions refuse `E_OFFLINE` (a lost action response can instead be
`pending`, retaining its retry ID). Observations follow normal online retention
and reconnect; ephemeral reads retain no offline hints. Signals drop rather than
replay. A new query can probe reconnect; the one-shot screen retries explicitly.
Without a device the arm is a restricted facade over the app's existing client,
with no second client, credential verification or write journal. In read-only
mode its writes/actions refuse `E_READ_ONLY`, and the original verified read
session expires without any SDK refresh. Shared epochs, principal sign-out
watermarks and `.read` custody retain their existing semantics.

The app's session state machine maintains these invariants under the shared
session lock:

- **I1 — stored bearer protection.** A runtime never sends revocation for the
  currently stored bearer. Explicit logout first commits a logout tombstone,
  then revokes the displaced sessions in the background. Logout compares its last
  committed principal under the lock: it owns that principal's credentials in
  every epoch, including newer logins, and preserves a different principal.
- **I2 — failure atomicity.** Failed sign-in, guest, replacement, refresh or
  logout preserves the session bytes and epoch. The sole logout intermediate
  state is a tombstone; every reader recognizes it as signed out.
- **I3 — retirement custody.** A server-minted bearer stays with its live
  runtime, the stored session, or a durable revocation obligation. Displacement
  is journaled before commit; revocations drain only after that commit. An
  acknowledgement retires the journal entry, including after restart.
- **I4 — principal isolation.** Once a runtime observes a changed epoch, it
  fences every older scope, including a provisional opening's rollback
  candidate, before notifying observers. It never adopts a different account
  without opening that account's client and outbox.
- **I5 — committed epochs.** An epoch advances with a committed replacement
  or logout, never with a failed operation.
- **I6 — coherent public identity.** Published auth state, viewer and client
  agree, including inside client notifications. Signed out exposes no live
  client; signed in exposes an open client for that viewer. Closing the current
  `app.client` also closes the app's public view and preserves the kept session.
- **I7 — refused session exclusion.** A server refusal conditionally replaces
  the still-stored bearer, or its known consumed predecessor after a failed
  rotation save, with a logout tombstone. Later opens, online or
  offline, stay signed out without opening that replica. An existing client
  loses access as soon as it learns the refusal. Cleanup cannot delete a
  different stored credential. Read sessions never rotate in the SDK.
  A transient failed refusal commit is retried
  once under the session lock; any remaining storage error is reported.
- **I8 — revoked public handles.** Hiding an account permanently fences every
  exposed client facade and its observations before notifying subscribers.
  Captured clients can no longer start reads, writes or refreshes, expose credentials or
  control the app lifecycle. The local client's existing `sync()` helper is
  also inert after its facade is hidden. Held observations return a refusal and notify
  their subscribers. Raw credentials needed for retry remain private. A failed
  replacement may restore the prior account through a new facade; it cannot
  reactivate any handle that was already hidden. This governs future access
  through handles, not copies of data or credentials already returned to code.
  Calls dispatched before the fence retain their raw outcomes (I12); query data
  and observation snapshots still require the live view when delivered.
- **I9 — global revocation.** A successful `logoutEverywhere()` acknowledges
  removal of every session of its principal at the server's revocation point,
  including other tabs, external sibling sessions and committed rotations whose
  responses have not arrived. It never selects another principal's credential.
  A deliberate new sign-in after that server operation creates a new session;
