```tsx
          const writes = sent.filter(write => ids.includes(write.id));
          assert(writes.length === 2 && writes[0]?.id === ids[0] && writes[0]!.seq < writes[1]!.seq);
          await w.receipt({ writes });
        });
      } finally { unsubscribe(); }
    };
    void run().catch(onError);
  }, [client, conversationId, onError]);
  return null;
}
```

Keep the actual chat screen visible: its observed query renders the two
pending bubbles while the runner waits. An assertion must throw before its
step completes. Add your own media, search or read-receipt assertions in the
same way; the tool imposes no application receipt schema.

```sh
xcrun simctl list devices available --json
# Set UDID to your dedicated, booted simulator's identifier.
npx expo run:ios --configuration Release --device "$UDID"
# Run from the backend project, with the app built for this backend origin.
npx snapback4 witness ios --bundle-id com.example.chat --udid "$UDID" \
  --segment offline --artifacts artifacts/offline --port 4400 --prime
```

The driver owns `snapback4 dev --port 4400 --no-watch`; stop any manually
started backend first. A bound port is refused, never reclaimed. `--udid` is
required with more than one booted iOS simulator. Without it exactly one
available booted iOS simulator must exist. `--timeout 120` is the default
number of seconds per driver step. The app's configured origin must be
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`; the kit does not change its client configuration.
A Release build embeds its JavaScript and needs no Metro server.
Quit the named app before starting: an already running instance is refused
with `E_WITNESS_APP`, and termination targets only the PID reported by the
driver's own launch, leaving a replacement instance running.

`--prime` first launches with `segment === "prime"`, waits for the completed
`primed` step, and terminates the app. It then stops the backend, verifies
connection refusal, starts video and logs, and cold-launches with the given
segment. Complete `offline-done`, await `waitFor("reconnect")`, then complete
`done`. `step(name, fn)` returns the function's result and records completion
only if it succeeds. Receipts inside a step carry `name:running`; failure
records `name:failed`. Steps are sequential. `receipt(object)` preserves the
object's fields and adds only `witness: { at, step }`; `witness` is reserved.
The helper serializes the app object before adding that envelope; custom
`toJSON` results must still be objects without `witness`.
`at` is an ISO timestamp. The helper appends and syncs each JSONL line in
Documents. The driver writes a run-specific reconnect file only after its
backend announces readiness again; container files require no simulator
network entitlement. Ordinary app launches cannot activate stale run files.

For the kill-and-relaunch variant, persist the two write IDs and bodies in
your app's storage. On the first offline launch complete `relaunch` after
asserting both are pending. On the second launch of the same segment read
the saved IDs and assert those exact pending rows survived, then complete
`offline-done`. Subscribe to `onWrite` on each launch before reconnect; wait
for both saved IDs to be `sent` in order, assert the visible rows, and complete
`done`. No extra sends belong on the second launch. Run that app scenario:

```sh
npx snapback4 witness ios --bundle-id com.example.chat --udid "$UDID" \
  --segment restart --artifacts artifacts/restart --port 4400 --prime --relaunch
```

Each run writes `<segment>-ios-screen.mp4` (uninterrupted native screen
recording), `<segment>-ios-receipts.jsonl` (the app's assertions and completed
steps), and `<segment>-ios-run.json` (simulator/runtime, installed Info.plist
build identifiers, backend command/origin/port, millisecond timestamps,
termination/relaunch events, byte counts, SHA-256 digests and exit status).
The device log and backend/capture logs accompany them. Missing or empty
artifacts, malformed receipts, failed steps, timeouts and backend failures
exit nonzero with an `E_WITNESS_*` diagnostic. Existing artifacts are never
overwritten; choose a fresh directory for a retry. Keep the manifest with
the exact video and receipt files it hashes.
A persistent `<segment>-ios-reserved` marker exclusively reserves all output
names; concurrent runs cannot share them, and backend/launch logs append
across restart and relaunch.
Every complete receipt is validated, including rows after a milestone and
again at collection; after `done`, only app receipts with the unchanged
`between-steps` state are accepted.

The manifest binds this execution's artifacts. It does not independently
verify the truth of application assertions, prove physical-device behavior,
simulate loss of every network connection, or establish media, search,
view-once exclusion or recipient `read` state unless your app asserts and
renders those observations. The deterministic simulator remains the main
engine harness; this witness covers native process, storage and UI boundaries.

## 8. Not in this release

Platform binaries other than darwin-arm64 (build from source with
`cargo build --release -p snapback4` and set `SNAPBACK4_BIN`), an Android
module, search beyond word prefixes (no stemming, relevance ranking,
phrase or mid-word matching), push delivery itself (a worker's, through
the effects above), an identity provider beyond guests, passwords,
services and the sessions a service mints, presence beyond the server's
own polls. If the package cannot express something, the diagnostic names
the term; record the gap and move on.


### Automatic delivery reports

A mutation declaring `reports delivery of messages by .conversation, .ordinal`
lets the SDK report exactly the positions delivered to this client. Local
clients persist debt with published confirmed rows and accepted fallback
manifests. Online clients collect accepted query manifests in memory, including
nested images. A composed answer omits the manifest when it replaces server
rows with retained local rows. Query manifests pass the same restore floor as
reports. Through `createApp` / `guardClient`, acceptance occurs only when the
facade publishes the shared authority-approved answer or returns it from
`query()` after approval. Its manifest follows the answer's identity, so peer
facades collect it once; refused, superseded or expired answers collect nothing.
Without a facade, acceptance remains the raw watch publication or query return,
synchronously at its final fences. Collection persistence never delays or rejects the answer;
every CAS attempt rechecks those fences, including at the host's commit point.
An answer overtaken before that write stays accepted, but collects nothing.
Unsupported conditional persistence also omits the collection; those rows stay
`sent`. No mounted conversation or application delivery hook is needed.
Keep calling `seen` for messages the person actually views. A continuously
mounted `progress` query acquires its returned message rows, so use it only
when that catch-up is intended.

Reports bypass the ordered outbox and dispatch only when its local network
chain is idle. Four groups may report concurrently, one call per binding and
group, with a 15-second deadline. A retained uncertain attempt keeps its id across
local restarts. Committed success covers its exact run; `RUNS_FULL` parks it
and allows other intervals to proceed. New publications, success, reconnect,
start and a slow timer wake parked runs, at most once per 30 seconds each.
Startup waits only for debt present at startup. Later activation pages wait
for capacity without evicting debt, retaining outbox priority even during live
traffic. A failed page resumes its durable cursor with bounded backoff.

`E_BOUND` is an ordinary non-retryable refusal in either the `why` or
`denied` envelope, including a denial without a head. The interval parks until
the next start and calls `onDeliveryRefused` once. Reconnect, timer wakes,
eviction and recollection do not resend it within the session; clean intervals
in the same group can still report. The next start retries with a new id.
An expired unswept backlog normally clears before then; if an oversized reply
hid a committed report, reporting that coverage again is a no-op. Retries are
bounded by app starts. Start-only suppression applies to every ordinary
non-retryable refusal, is scoped to fingerprint and group, and clears on start
or store reset; it creates no terminal refused entry.

Pass `onDeliveryRefused` to `createClient`, `createLocalClient` or `createApp`
for application refusals. It receives
`{ table, mutation, args, group, from, through, why }`; `why` is the ordinary
coded refusal. `NOT_A_RUN` and `PAST_LAST_MESSAGE` enter a remembered refused
set; other non-retryable application refusals park until restart.
`RUNS_FULL`, membership loss, auth pauses and transport retries do not emit
this callback. Reports do not appear in `onWrite` or `pendingWrites()`.

Local debt survives closing or sign-out for the same viewer. Online sign-out
waits at most one second for reports already in flight; remaining memory debt
is lost. Leaving drops a group's debt. Store replacement or detected restore
clears delivery metadata and fences outstanding callbacks; recover using a
fresh device store. Debt never crosses viewers or binding incarnations.
Each report sends `delivery: { fingerprint }` from its compiled binding or
manifest. `E_DELIVERY_BINDING` drops that binding's state; an unrelated backend
generation preserves unchanged fingerprints. Positions outside JavaScript's
safe-integer range are never collected.

Each binding/group keeps at most 256 owed intervals, 256 reported intervals
and 64 refused intervals. There are at most 4,096 local or 1,024 online active
groups. Eviction drops owed positions, which stay `sent`, but retains refused
intervals. A saturated refused set stops that group's collection and dispatch
until a leave/rejoin or a new device store.

### Inspect subscription pressure

If a screen flashes empty, compare queue/in-flight counts with withdrawal causes.
A `change-timeout` exhausts the answer's one-second budget outside capacity wait;
expiry, denial and resets remain immediate. The last 256 completed attempts supply
queue/attempt latency p50/p95/max, and the last 64 withdrawals retain causes.
Samples contain query names and counts, never arguments or answer values.

```tsx
import type { Client } from "snapback4/contract";
import { inspect } from "snapback4/inspection";
import { useInspection } from "snapback4/react";

export function logSubscriptions(client: Client) {
  const pressure = inspect(client);
  console.table(pressure.queries);
  console.table(pressure.recentWithdrawals);
}
export function SubscriptionPressure({ development }: { development: boolean }) {
  const pressure = useInspection(development);
  return pressure ? <pre>{JSON.stringify(pressure.totals, null, 2)}</pre> : null;
}
```

Mount the overlay inside the client provider and pass the host's development flag
(`import.meta.env.DEV`, or `__DEV__` in Expo). Disabled installs no timer; enabled
samples every 250 ms. Counts include lingering observations and delayed retries;
direct reads and presence refreshes are outside this queue.


### Visible seen progress and independent history

After `check`, a receipts clause emits `api.receiptFamilies.chat`. Import
`useSeen` from `snapback4/react` on web or native:

```tsx
import { usePage, useSeen } from "snapback4/react";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";

export function useReceiptScreen(id: string, visibleIds: ReadonlySet<string>, foreground: boolean) {
  const history = usePage(api.history, { conversation: id });
  const through = Math.max(0, ...history.items.filter(m => visibleIds.has(m.id) && !m.pending).map(m => m.ordinal));
  const seen = useSeen(api.receiptFamilies.chat, { scope: id, through, active: foreground });
  const decorations = usePage(api.messageReceipts, { conversation: id });
  return { history, seen, decorations };
}
```

Supply viewport IDs from the platform's actual visibility callbacks; intersect
with current confirmed rows and combine route focus with foreground. Reset IDs
on account/backend/scope change. Loaded history and acquisition do not mean seen.
Match current decorations by ID; their denial or loading never removes retained
history and grants no media authority. These reads are independent snapshots.

The hook shares progress and one admission/pending call per mounted
client/family/scope. Member withdrawals, replacement, session and store/generation
resets discard local progress; final unmount drops unadmitted progress. Admitted
writes remain in the SDK outbox through restart. The hook never pages history,
reads catch-up progress, or reports delivery. The descriptor's typed member/seen
handles, actual argument names, mapping and fingerprint come from the compiler.

`seen.state` is idle/admitting/pending/retrying/failed; `seen.through` is local
progress, never a confirmed receipt. `seen.why` exposes refusals. Known
E_ADMISSION/E_ADMISSION_STORE/E_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT failures retry with 1–60-second
backoff, at most eight retries while active. Reconnect or `seen.retry()` after
repair wakes those refusals. Other failures/unknown outcomes remember the rejected
position and reset local progress to `max(joining floor, acknowledged)` before failing.
A later different visible position above that floor starts a new attempt, even
below the rejected position. Repeated input and retry never resubmit the rejected
position; membership/session reset clears it.
See `snapback4 guide receipts` for the full rules and two-read recipe.

### Refused sessions and dev time tests

`E_AUTH` retains family `auth` and the server's message on the local tier,
online tier and app online arm, including calls after terminal refusal. Detailed
dev explanations require the dev-only endpoint trust check (loopback peer, Host and
browser Origin). A remaining record can identify expiry; absent records may mean an
earlier/replaced store, another instance, expiry or sign-out, including before server
startup. No token history is kept. Sign in again and discard saved earlier-store tokens.
Serve and untrusted dev requests, including public POST routes, use the same generic
"this session is not live; sign in again" for each case. Clients without credentials
still ask you to sign in. There is no new refusal field; avoid matching message text.
Refused session tokens on logout, narrow, refresh and logout-all use the same
HTTP 401 and `guide: personas` envelope as data requests, without a code prefix
inside the message. Device-app restoration keeps its terminal refusal on
`app.ready`, `app.auth.why` and the signed-out `app.online` query/mutate/act facade.
Local `logoutAll` preserves an already retained refusal; a new sign-in replaces it.

For time-travel tests use `snapback4 dev --fresh --port 4401`, point the suite's
client URL at `http://127.0.0.1:4401`, then run `snapback4 clock advance 25h --port 4401`.
Stop that disposable server after the suite. Each new store needs new sessions.
The advance reports its cumulative offset and restart lifetime. `doctor --url
http://127.0.0.1:4401` reports that clock; dev startup and doctor flag future stamps
in the latest 64 commits with `N_CLOCK_STORE_AHEAD`. Older commits can be missed,
even when their rows remain; historical commit stamps can outlive deleted rows. See `snapback4 guide jobs` for the
complete recipe and detection scope. Inspection failures print "unavailable" and
leave dev startup running; ordinary store admission still applies. No row image
is inspected. Restarting resets time, not written rows.

### Durable media capture

A local device owns captured bytes and the placing mutation across offline/reload.
`useUpload` exposes that same custody in React. See [OFFLINE-UPLOADS.md](./OFFLINE-UPLOADS.md) for states and limits.

```tsx
import { useUpload } from "snapback4/react";
import { hasUploads, uploadAndPlace, blobArrayBuffer } from "snapback4/local";
import type { Client } from "snapback4/contract";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api.ts";

export async function capturePhoto(client: Client, photo: Blob) {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await blobArrayBuffer(photo));
  if (hasUploads(client)) return uploadAndPlace(client, api.sendPhoto, { conversationId: "c" }, bytes, { argument: "photo" });
}
export function PhotoCapture({ photo }: { photo: Blob }) {
  const upload = useUpload(api.sendPhoto, "photo");
  return <button disabled={!upload.available} onClick={() => upload.uploadAndPlace({ conversationId: "c" }, photo)}>{upload.state?.state ?? "Send photo"}</button>;
}
```

### Device build identity

Every wasm producer linking `snapback4-device` receives a `snapback4.engine` custom section from the crate. Its `{format:1, version, capabilities}` agrees with `engine_info`, available before partition open. Native hosts expose the same identity; Rust adapters use `engine::headers()` and forward `x-snapback-device` with schema, sync and changes requests. Exact's JSON sidecar and the package's engine JSON sidecar are derived diagnostics. `check` and Exact preflight read the embedded identity and compare the server's public-projection floor and capabilities. A package version or sidecar cannot substitute for it.

The application client declarations typecheck with ES2022 and WebWorker libraries without DOM or Node globals. The Node-only proof subpath uses Node and browser DOM types. Custom session mirrors implement the structural `StorageLike` interface from `snapback4/auth`.

### Application proofs in Node

`snapback4/proof` runs in Node with Playwright browser types; application client
imports remain usable with ES2022/WebWorker types alone. Use the generated
`frontend:proof` first; `guide testing` shows the short browser recipe. A custom
proof can compose the same bounded hosts, private logs and saved release inputs:

```ts
import { startDev, startServe, startStatic, startVite, cli, command, deploy,
  rollback, testSource, withBrowser, waitForFresh, waitForClock, fillRN, statusText,
  selectByValue, renderedText, frontPage, logsDir, bounded, cleanup, stopChild, portRange, sandboxUnavailable, loadFixtures }
  from "snapback4/proof";

export async function applicationProof(cwd: string) {
  const options = { cwd, logsDir: logsDir(), timeoutMs: 120_000 };
  console.log("proof port range", portRange());
  const checked = await cli(["check"], options);
  if (checked.code !== 0) throw Error(checked.stderr);
  const acceptance = await testSource("versions/v1.q", options);
  if (acceptance.code !== 0) throw Error(acceptance.stderr);
  await deploy("deployment", "versions/v1.q", options);
  const backend = await startServe("deployment", options);
  try {
    const build = await command("npm", ["run", "build"], options);
    if (build.code !== 0) throw Error(build.stderr);
    const frontend = await startStatic("dist", options);
    try {
      await withBrowser({ cwd }, async context => {
        const page = await context.newPage();
        await page.goto(`${frontend.url}/?api=${encodeURIComponent(backend.url)}`);
        const status = statusText(page), before = await status.textContent();
        await fillRN(page.getByLabel("Title"), "Proof");
        await selectByValue(page.getByLabel("Category"), "work");
        await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Add" }).click();
        await bounded(waitForFresh(status, before), 35_000, "fresh rendered result");
        await renderedText(page, "Proof", { within: page.getByRole("list") }).waitFor();
        await frontPage(page);
      });
    } finally { await stopChild(frontend); }
    await deploy("deployment", "versions/v2.q", options);
    await rollback("deployment", 1, options);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(sandboxUnavailable(error) ? "browser sandbox unavailable" : "proof failed");
    throw error;
  } finally { await cleanup(() => backend.stop()); }
}

// Development hosts use the same custody. Add assertions before stopping them.
export async function developmentHosts(cwd: string) {
  const backend = await startDev({ cwd, args: ["--memory", "--unsafe-dev-doors"] });
  try {
    // Read the application's fixtures/<table>.jsonl using the dev schema/clock.
    const seed = await loadFixtures("fixtures", { url: backend.url, cwd });
    const response = await fetch(`${backend.url}/seed`, { method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(seed) });
    const result = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok || result.denied) throw Error(JSON.stringify(result));
    const frontend = await startVite(cwd);
    await cleanup(() => frontend.stop());
  } finally { await cleanup(() => backend.stop()); }
}

// Pass a signed-in page with a registered witness after a dev clock advance.
export async function advancedPageClock(page: import("playwright-core").Page, advanced: { now: number }) {
  return waitForClock(page, advanced.now);
}
```


### Poll authoritative projection after settlement

After asserting a write's sent receipt, a proof can wait for its server-backed
projection. A deadline reports the last answer and never declares a write failed.

```ts
import type { Online } from "snapback4/app";
import { waitForServer } from "snapback4/proof";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
export async function committedNote(online: Online, id: string) {
  return waitForServer(() => online.query(api.staffNotes, {team:"proof"}),
    read => "data" in read && read.fresh && read.data.some(row => row.id === id),
    {label:"committed note"});
}
```


## Password React and Expo

Beside the persona form (`guide personas`), use this for `use identity password`:
```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { createApp } from "snapback4/app";
import { localStorageSessionStore } from "snapback4/auth";
import { AppProvider, useAuth } from "snapback4/react";
const app = createApp({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:4400", sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore() });
export function PasswordApp() { return <AppProvider app={app}><Password /></AppProvider>; }
function Password() {
  const auth = useAuth(), [email, setEmail] = useState(""), [password, setPassword] = useState(""), [why, setWhy] = useState("");
  if (auth.state === "restoring") return <>Restoring…</>;
  if (auth.state === "signed-in") return <>Signed in as {auth.viewer}</>;
  const submit = async (signup: boolean) => { const r = await (signup ? auth.signup(email, password) : auth.login(email, password)); if (!r.ok) setWhy(r.why.message); };
  return <><input aria-label="Email" value={email} onChange={e => setEmail(e.target.value)} /><input aria-label="Password" type="password" value={password} onChange={e => setPassword(e.target.value)} />
    <button onClick={() => void submit(false)}>Sign in</button><button onClick={() => void submit(true)}>Sign up</button>{why}</>;
}
```
Sign-in: {ok:true, session} or {ok:false, why}. useAuth exposes no session. Expo: secureStoreSessionStore(SecureStore); web: localStorageSessionStore. guide production.

`useAuth()` members: `state`, `viewer`, `why`, `signup(email, password)`, `login(email, password)`, `guest()`, `logout()`, `logoutEverywhere()`.
`signOut()` belongs to the client, not useAuth. Install `expo-secure-store` with `npx expo install expo-secure-store`, then:
```ts

const app = createApp({url: "http://127.0.0.1:4400", device: nativeDevice, sessionStore: secureStoreSessionStore(SecureStore)});
```
Storage failures propagate. Rebuild.


## Shared list and write props
```tsx
import { matchReadList, readPresentation, type PageHook, type WriteHook } from "snapback4/react";
export function SharedList<T extends {id: string}>({page, remove, label}: {page: PageHook<T[]>; remove: WriteHook<{id: string}, unknown>; label: (row: T) => string}) { const status = readPresentation(page.read); return <>{matchReadList(page.read, {denied: why => <p role="alert">{why.message}</p>,
    otherwise: () => <p>{status.incomplete ? "Incomplete results" : "Waiting or empty"}</p>,
    present: () => <ul>{page.items.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{label(row)}<button disabled={remove.inFlight} onClick={() => void remove.run({id: row.id})}>Remove</button></li>)}</ul>})}
    {status.incomplete && <p>More rows may exist</p>}{remove.last?.state === "failed" && <p role="alert">{remove.last.why.message}</p>}
    <button disabled={!page.hasMore} onClick={page.loadMore}>More</button></>; }
```
Pass usePage(api.list) and useMutation(api.remove). Match page.read, render page.items. `absent` can be an authorised empty list; query myMembership for roles. createClient takes generated handles (api.op), never names.

## List read state

`ReadState` from snapback4/react renders a list read or `usePage` result in one
expression. Loading/empty default to null; omitted denied throws QueryRefusal.
Empty describes returned rows, including partial/stale lists, not proven absence.
The data renderer receives the same precise read metadata. Supply Text/View
slots in React Native; the component creates no observation or retained state.

```tsx
import { ReadState, type Read } from "snapback4/react";
export function ListScreen({ read }: { read: Read<readonly { id: string; title: string }[]> }) {
  return <ReadState read={read} loading={<p>Loading…</p>} empty={<p>No results</p>} denied={why => <p role="alert">{why.message}</p>}>{(rows, answer) => <ul data-complete={answer.complete}>{rows.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title}</li>)}</ul>}</ReadState>;
}
```

## Short screens

`useQueryData(op,args)` returns data or undefined while loading. Refusals throw
`QueryRefusal` (its `why` is a typed Refusal) for an error boundary. For an inline
refusal use `useQueryResult`; `read` retains the full metadata. Both show partial
and stale data as it arrives: use `useQuery`/`usePage` when completeness, freshness
or pagination matters. Null, false, zero and empty lists remain data. Arguments
are inferred from the generated operation. `SignedIn` mounts children only after
sign-in; restoration defaults to null. Place it inside AppProvider.

```tsx
import { SignedIn, useQueryData, useQueryResult } from "snapback4/react";
import { api } from "../snapback/generated/api";
export function QuickNotes({team}:{team:string}) {
  const rows = useQueryData(api.staffNotes, {team});
  return rows === undefined ? <p>Loading…</p> : <ul>{rows.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title}</li>)}</ul>;
}
export function InlineNotes({team}:{team:string}) {
  const {data,why} = useQueryResult(api.staffNotes, {team});
  return why ? <p role="alert">{why.message}</p> : data === undefined ? <p>Loading…</p> : <ul>{data.map(row => <li key={row.id}>{row.title}</li>)}</ul>;
}
export function ShortScreen() {
  return <SignedIn fallback={<p>Sign in</p>} restoring={<p>Restoring…</p>}><InlineNotes team="t" /></SignedIn>;
}
```

## Money arguments from JavaScript

`money USD` defaults to scale 2: pass integer cents, so 1234 is $12.34.
`decimal 4` likewise uses integers scaled by 10,000. Fractions such as 12.34
refuse E_INPUT; the SDK does not silently round. Declare this as
`snapback/money.q`, then run check to generate its module handle:

```quarry
table prices:
  owner: principal
  amount: money USD
  immutable owner
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  online only
mutation recordPrice(amount: money USD):
  return insert prices { owner: viewer, amount }
```

In a Node 24 module at the project root, use the generated operation exactly
as in a React handler. Pass your authenticated client to this helper:

```js
import { api } from "./snapback/generated/api.ts";
export function recordPrice(client) {
  return client.mutate(api.money.recordPrice, { amount: 1234 });
}
```


### Bounded identity retries and local production shutdown (0.4.35)

SDK `guest`, `signup`, and `login` accept `timeoutMs` (default 180000) and
`signal` alongside `scope`. Only an explicit HTTP 429 auth E_RATE_LIMIT refusal
retries, at most four attempts, waiting `retryAfterMs` or an older server's
Retry-After header. Requests preserve credentials/scope; lost replies and session
rotation are never replayed. Proof `seedAccounts` uses the same retry path and
its remaining five-minute setup budget. A too-long wait returns the refusal
(or E_STAGING_TIMEOUT for setup), preserving the server delay.

`startServe().stop()` resolves after its retained native child exits and the
kernel store lock is released, including worker cleanup. Concurrent/repeated
stops coalesce. Cleanup failure rejects. `serve DIR --wait-stopped` exposes the
five-second read-only lock barrier; it never signals a PID or initializes a
store. Deploy/rollback also wait before admission for a shutting-down owner;
live serve still uses authenticated control. Ambiguous activation is not retried.

`data TABLE --json` now returns `{rows, more, limit}` including empty results.
The default limit is 50. Check `more` before interpreting a row count; increase
`--limit N` for a larger inspection. Text output stays JSON lines. This replaces
the previous bare JSON array so stdout-only callers can detect truncation.

fn period(schedule: &snapback4_core::schema::Schedule) -> String {
    schedule.describe()
}

/// What each schedule did on one clock advance, and why one did not fire.
/// The core fires each schedule at most once per advance, for the latest
/// boundary, and holds it while its saved boundary is ahead of the clock.
// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — missed boundaries fire once; this only explains them.
pub fn schedule_report(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], fired: &[String], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool, port: Option<u16>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let after = saved_boundaries(engine);
    // Read only bounded summaries: job args/cursors and full error payloads
    // are irrelevant to this report and must not be loaded then replicated.
    let runs = job_summaries(engine).unwrap_or_default();
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| {
        let (old, saved) = (before.get(index).copied().flatten(), after.get(index).copied().flatten());
        let current = schedule.boundary(now);
        let next = schedule.next(current);
        let mut entry = serde_json::json!({ "name": schedule.name, "target": schedule.target, "period": period(schedule), "fired": false, "firedWindows": [], "skippedBoundaries": [], "nextBoundary": utc(next) });
        if fired.contains(&schedule.name) {
            let end = saved.unwrap_or(current);
            entry["fired"] = true.into();
            let start = schedule.previous(end);
            let window = |boundary| serde_json::json!({"periodStart": schedule.previous(boundary), "periodEnd": boundary});
            let mut windows = Vec::new();
            if each_boundary {
                if let Some(old) = old {
                    let mut at = schedule.next(old);
                    while at <= end { windows.push(window(at)); at = schedule.next(at); }
                }
            } else { windows.push(window(end)); }
            if each_boundary {
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired {} windows: {}", windows.len(), windows.iter().map(|window| format!("{} to {}", utc(window["periodStart"].as_i64().unwrap()), utc(window["periodEnd"].as_i64().unwrap()))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ")).into();
            }
            entry["firedWindows"] = windows.into();
            entry["periodStart"] = start.into();
            entry["periodEnd"] = end.into();
            if !each_boundary { entry["reason"] = format!("fired for the period {} to {}", utc(start), utc(end)).into(); }
            if let Some(run) = runs.get(&schedule.target) { entry["run"] = run.clone(); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.040#24-monthly-and-yearly-schedules — calendar periods count boundaries, not milliseconds.
            let skipped = if each_boundary { 0 } else { old.map(|old| schedule.periods_between(old, end) - 1).unwrap_or(0) };
            if skipped > 0 {
                entry["skippedPeriods"] = skipped.into();
                let mut windows = Vec::new();
                let mut at = schedule.next(old.unwrap());
                while at < end && windows.len() < SKIPPED_PREVIEW {
                    let mut item = window(at);
                    let mut args = serde_json::Map::new();
                    if let Some(program) = engine.program(&schedule.target) {
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") { args.insert("periodStart".into(), schedule.previous(at).into()); }
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") { args.insert("periodEnd".into(), at.into()); }
                    }
                    item["command"] = format!("snapback4 run {} '{}'{}", schedule.target, serde_json::Value::Object(args), port.map(|port| format!(" --port {port}")).unwrap_or_default()).into();
                    windows.push(item); at = schedule.next(at);
                }
                entry["skippedBoundariesOmitted"] = (skipped - windows.len() as i64).into();
                entry["skippedBoundaries"] = windows.into();
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired once, for the latest period {} to {}; {skipped} earlier period{} this advance crossed (from {}) did not run: missed boundaries fire once. Run {} with periodStart/periodEnd for an earlier period",
                    utc(start), utc(end), if skipped == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, utc(old.unwrap_or(end)), schedule.target).into();
            }
        } else if held {
            entry["holdCode"] = "disabled".into();
            entry["reason"] = "schedules are held (dev --hold-schedules or --replay); a restart without the flag resumes at the next boundary".into();
        } else if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| old.is_some() && (*saved > current || *saved == current && *saved > schedule.boundary(snapback4_core::now_ms()))) {
            let due = schedule.next(saved);
            entry["holdCode"] = "saved-boundary".into();
            entry["savedBoundary"] = saved.into();
            entry["heldUntil"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["nextBoundary"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("held by the store: boundary {} was already processed and this clock {} has not reached its next window (restarting resets the process offset, not the saved boundary). One fire per boundary. Advance {} more, or use a fresh staging deployment/store for an independent test; keep the same --clock-offset when continuing a test across serve restarts",
                utc(saved), utc(now), span(due - now)).into();
        } else if old != saved {
            entry["holdCode"] = "initialized".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("{} started at boundary {}: a schedule fires at the boundary after the first one it sees, next {} ({} from now)",
                if old.is_none() { "this schedule" } else { "this changed schedule" }, utc(saved.unwrap_or(current)), utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        } else {
            entry["holdCode"] = "not-due".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("next boundary {} ({} from now; schedule times are UTC)", utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        }
        entry
    }).collect()
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — every declared schedule has one reported outcome.
pub fn outcomes(schedules: &[serde_json::Value]) -> (Vec<serde_json::Value>, Vec<serde_json::Value>) {
    schedules.iter().cloned().partition(|schedule| schedule["fired"] == true)
}

/// The report never loads full error/argument payloads from retained jobs.
fn job_summaries(engine: &Engine) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut summaries = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for summary in engine.store().job_summaries(REPORT_ERROR_BYTES)? {
        let name = summary.name;
        if summaries.contains_key(&name) { continue; }
        let mut error = summary.error;
        let truncated = summary.error_truncated;
        if let Some(text) = &mut error && truncated {
            let mut end = REPORT_ERROR_BYTES.min(text.len());
            while !text.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }
            text.truncate(end); text.push('…');
        }
        summaries.insert(name, serde_json::json!({ "id":summary.id, "state":summary.state,
            "rowsWritten":summary.rows_written, "error":error, "errorTruncated":truncated }));

// Reset even when a debug/unwind request panics mid-drain. Engine poison
// recovery and durable work cursors retain the normal retry semantics.
struct Advancing<'a>(&'a Shared);
impl Drop for Advancing<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let mut state = lock(&self.0.maintenance);
        state.advancing = false;
        state.next = BulkKind::Delivery;
    }
}

fn completed_drain(work: Work, stopping: bool) -> Result<Work, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    if stopping {
        return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INTERRUPTED", "clock", "clock advanced, but host shutdown interrupted the drain; inspect queued work instead of repeating the advance").guide("clock"));
    }
    Ok(work)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#4-staging-clock — staging grants clock control, never fixture or persona authority.
pub(super) fn staging(shared: &Shared) -> bool {
    lock(&shared.engine).store().meta("deployment_environment").ok().flatten().as_deref() == Some("staging")
}
fn clock_service(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Result<Option<String>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    if shared.personas { return Ok(None); }
    if !staging(shared) { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
    match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
        Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Ok(Some(principal)),
        _ => Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "staging clock control requires a full service token").guide("clock")),
    }
}
pub(super) fn advance(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    let service = match clock_service(&request, shared) {
        Ok(service) => service,
        Err(why) => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})),
    };
    let payload = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(body) {
        Ok(payload) => payload,
        Err(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))})),
    };
    let each_boundary = match payload.get("eachBoundary") {
        None => false,
        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(value)) => *value,
        Some(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("eachBoundary must be a boolean"))})),
    };
    let duration = payload.get("duration").and_then(|value| value.as_str());
    let milliseconds = match duration.ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))
        .and_then(crate::dev_clock::duration) {
        Ok(milliseconds) => milliseconds,
        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    };
    // Serialize clock callers only. Background slices check advancing after
    // engine admission and skip during this synchronous drain.
    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
    let _advance = lock(&advance);
    let _advancing = Advancing(shared);
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — simulated time makes retries due without stealing a live worker's claim or viewer session.
    let advanced = (|| {
        // Match claims' engine-then-clock lock order: no claim can land
        // between shifting its lease and publishing the advanced clock.
        let mut engine = lock(&shared.engine);
        let before = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(&engine);
        if let Some(principal) = &service {
            if engine.store().meta("deployment_environment").map_err(|e|e.refusal())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
            super::session_identity::mutation_authority(&request,shared,&engine,principal)?;
        } else { shared.dev_authority(&engine)?; }
        let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock);
        let mut next = clock.clone();
        let now = next.advance(milliseconds)?.max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire));
        let boundaries = crate::dev_clock_store::crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary)?;
        lock(&shared.maintenance).advancing = true;
        engine.advance_worker_leases_at(milliseconds, clock.now()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?;
        *clock = next;
        let offset = clock.offset();
        let skew = now - snapback4_core::now_ms();
        let isolated = if crate::dev_clock_store::has_data(&engine) {
            format!("; use {} for isolated time tests; clock advance --port N targets its printed port (guide jobs)", crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())
        } else { String::new() };
        let message = format!("cumulative offset {offset:+}ms (requested process offset; now includes the authoritative floor); process offset lasts until restart{isolated}");
        Ok((now, offset, skew, message, before, boundaries))
    })();
    let (now, offset, skew, message, before, boundaries) = match advanced {
        Ok(result) => result,
        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    };
    // @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — a developer is awaiting this
    // request; synchronous clock-advance work intentionally keeps request QoS.
    let drained = (|| {
        let mut crossed = Vec::new();
        if each_boundary {
            for (index, at) in boundaries {
                crossed.extend(engine_work(shared, |engine, _| engine.fire_schedule_boundary_at(shared.now(), index, at))?);
            }
        }
        let mut work = work_at(shared, true, 0, Some(now))?;
        work.schedules += crossed.len();
        work.fired.extend(crossed);
        Ok::<_, RuntimeError>(work)
    })();
    match drained.map_err(|error| error.refusal()).and_then(|work| completed_drain(work, crate::lifecycle::stopping())) {
        Ok(work) => {
            let schedules = crate::dev_clock_store::schedule_report(&lock(&shared.engine), &before, &work.fired, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary, shared.dev_identity.as_ref().map(|i| i.address.port()));
            let (fired, held) = crate::dev_clock_store::outcomes(&schedules);
            respond(request, 200, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "sessionNotice":crate::dev_clock::SESSION_NOTICE, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":skew, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "work":work, "schedules":schedules, "fired":fired, "held":held}))
        }
        // Time remains advanced if maintenance fails; callers must not
        // retry the advance blindly. The normal tick retries pending work.
        Err(error) => {
            let engine = lock(&shared.engine);
            let after = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(&engine);
            let fired: Vec<_> = engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().filter(|(i, _)| {
                matches!((before.get(*i).copied().flatten(), after.get(*i).copied().flatten()), (Some(old), Some(new)) if new > old)
            }).map(|(_, schedule)| schedule.name.clone()).collect();
            let mut schedules = crate::dev_clock_store::schedule_report(&engine, &before, &fired, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary, shared.dev_identity.as_ref().map(|i| i.address.port()));
            for (index, schedule) in schedules.iter_mut().enumerate() {
                if schedule["fired"] != true && !shared.hold_schedules && before.get(index).copied().flatten().is_some_and(|old| old < engine.schema().schedules[index].boundary(now)) {
                    schedule["holdCode"] = "maintenance-failed".into();
                    schedule["reason"] = "clock advanced but maintenance stopped before this due boundary was queued; inspect clock and queued jobs before continuing; do not replay the advance".into();
                }
            }
            let (fired, held) = crate::dev_clock_store::outcomes(&schedules);
            respond(request, 500, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "sessionNotice":crate::dev_clock::SESSION_NOTICE, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":skew, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "schedules":schedules, "fired":fired, "held":held, "reportIncomplete":true, "denied":refusal_json(&error)}))
        },
    }
}

/// `POST /dev/jobs/<job>` with `{"args":{..}}`: queue one run of a job as the
/// system on the dev clock and drive chunks until it is done or parked. This is
/// what `snapback4 run <job>` forwards to while dev owns the store.
pub(super) fn run_job(request: Request, shared: &Shared, name: &str, body: &str) {
    use snapback4_core::{JobState, error::Refusal, ir::ProgramKind, wire};
    let service_route=request.url().starts_with("/jobs/");
    let service=if service_route {
        match super::session_identity::principal_of(&request,shared) {
            Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind=="service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Some(principal),
            _ => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH","auth","triggering a deployed system job requires a full service token").guide("jobs"))})),
        }
    } else {
        if !shared.personas {return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH","auth","/dev/jobs is a development door; use run <job> --release <dir> with a service token").guide("jobs"))}));}
        None
    };

//! Compile examples and audit source diagnostic coverage.
use super::*;

pub(super) fn compile(source: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
    snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".to_owned(), source.to_owned())])
}

pub(super) fn clean(label: &str, source: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
    let bound = compile(source);
    let list = |items: &[snapback4_lang::Diagnostic]| items.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{label} does not compile:\n{}", list(&bound.diagnostics));
    // DX5 makes reader-only gates and private named conflicts visible in
    // existing examples. They remain runnable; pin the source and repair of
    // each advisory rather than calling an intentional privacy gate unclean.
    for note in bound.notes.iter().filter(|n| matches!(n.code.as_str(), "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED" | "N_UNIQUE_HIDDEN")) {
        let line = source.lines().nth(note.site.line.saturating_sub(1) as usize).expect("located source advice");
        assert_eq!(note.guide, "rules");
        assert!(note.rewrite.contains("private rows") && !note.rewrite.is_empty(), "{note}");
        if note.code == "N_UNIQUE_HIDDEN" { assert!(line.contains("unique"), "{line}: {note}"); }
        else { assert!(line.contains('[') || line.trim_start().starts_with("receipts "), "{line}: {note}"); }
    }
    let notes = if source.contains(&guide::language()) { guide_context::without_grouped_shape_note(&bound, "groupedMessages") }
        else { bound.notes.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>() };
    let notes: Vec<_> = notes.into_iter().filter(|n| !matches!(n.code.as_str(), "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED" | "N_UNIQUE_HIDDEN")).collect();
    // The populated-store feed deliberately teaches its sparse-scan limit.
    // Pin the actual card block and its one note; other examples stay clean.
    if quarry(card("feeds").unwrap()).iter().any(|block| block == source && block.contains("query home(") && !block.contains("view following:")) {
        assert_eq!(notes.len(), 1, "{label}: {:?}", bound.notes);
        assert_eq!(notes[0].code, "N_SPARSE_FILTER");
        return bound;
    }
    if quarry(card("offline-interactions").unwrap()).iter().any(|block| block == source && block.contains("view ownLikes:")) {
        assert_eq!((notes.len(), notes.first().map(|n| n.code.as_str())), (1, Some("N_MAINTAIN_SYNCED")), "{label}: {:?}", bound.notes);
        return bound;
    }
    // These exact published ordinary-search examples teach both coverage notes.
    // Keep their codes, counts and query site pinned; no general note exemption.
    let search_examples = quarry(card("search").unwrap());
    let package_examples = quarry(include_str!("../../../../packages/snapback4/README.md"));
    if search_examples.iter().skip(1).chain(package_examples.iter())
        .any(|block| block == source && block.contains("query search(q: text <=100, c: cursor ?):")) {
        let notes = if source.contains("query searchGrouped(") { guide_context::without_grouped_shape_note(&bound, "searchGrouped") } else { notes };
        let mut codes = notes.iter().map(|note| note.code.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        codes.sort_unstable();
        assert_eq!(codes, ["N_NEVER_COMPLETE", "N_SYNC_ORDER"], "{label}: {:?}", bound.notes);
        assert!(notes.iter().all(|note| note.message.starts_with("query search")), "{label}: {:?}", bound.notes);
        return bound;
    }
    // The timed-peer recipe intentionally preserves a hidden-target upsert's
    // runtime deadline equality. Pin its one documented uncertainty, not a
    // general immutable-note exemption.
    if quarry(card("rule-recipes").unwrap()).iter().any(|block| block == source
        && block.contains("mutation reportWords(") && block.contains("table peerCounts:")) {
        assert_eq!(notes.len(), 1, "{label}: {:?}", bound.notes);
        let note = &notes[0];
        assert_eq!(note.code, "N_IMMUTABLE_PATCH");
        assert!(note.message.contains("peerCounts.opensAt"), "{note:?}");
        assert!(note.message.contains("equals the stored value"), "{note:?}");
        assert!(card("rule-recipes").unwrap().contains("runtime equality"));
        return bound;
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#14 — caller-visible existence is the lesson, not global absence.
    // This exact ladder example intentionally contrasts a hidden rule probe
    // with caller-visible existence; its one advisory note is part of the lesson.

        return bound;

    // The live recipe deliberately teaches its full-current acquisition note.
    if source.contains("table liveRosterFiles:") {
        assert_eq!(notes.len(),1,"{label}: {:?}",bound.notes);
        assert_eq!(notes[0].code,"N_NO_HORIZON");
        assert!(notes[0].rewrite.contains("online only") && !notes[0].rewrite.contains("last 500"));
        return bound;
    }
    let unexpected: Vec<_> = notes.into_iter().filter(|note| !matches!(note.code.as_str(), "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED" | "N_UNIQUE_HIDDEN") && !(source.contains("ephemeral ") && note.code == "N_EPHEMERAL_SERVER")).cloned().collect();
    assert!(unexpected.is_empty(), "{label} compiles with notes:\n{}", list(&unexpected));
    bound
}

/// The sources a scan of literals covers: the Rust crates and the client.
pub(super) fn sources() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    let root = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..");
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    fn walk(dir: &Path, files: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("{}: {e}", dir.display())) {
            let path = entry.unwrap().path();
            if path.is_dir() {
                if path.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n == "node_modules" || n == "target" || n == "dist" || n == "tests" || n == "test") {
                    continue;
                }
                // Differential-test records quote the Lean model's own
                // refusals (`E_MODEL_TYPE`), which no product path emits.
                if path.ends_with("snapback4-difftest/cases") {
                    continue;
                }
                walk(&path, files);
            } else if path.file_name().is_some_and(|n| n.to_string_lossy().ends_with("_tests.rs") || n.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".test.mjs")) {
                // A test module inside `src/` invents refusal codes for fixtures;
                // this check is about the codes the product itself emits.
                continue;
            } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == "rs" || e == "ts" || e == "tsx" || e == "md") {
                files.push(path);
            }
        }
    }
    for dir in ["crates", "packages/snapback4/src", "packages/snapback4-expo/src"] {
        walk(&root.join(dir), &mut files);
    }
    files.push(root.join("packages/snapback4/README.md"));
    assert!(files.len() > 40, "{} source files", files.len());
    files
}

/// Product and feed-recipe codes at identifier boundaries, including extracted Markdown cards.
fn code_words(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
    let ident = |b: u8| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_';
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i + 2 < bytes.len() {
        let prefix = [b"E_".as_slice(), b"N_".as_slice(), b"FEED_".as_slice()].into_iter().find(|p| bytes[i..].starts_with(p));
        if let Some(prefix) = prefix.filter(|p| bytes.get(i + p.len()).is_some_and(u8::is_ascii_uppercase) && (i == 0 || !ident(bytes[i - 1]))) {
            let start = i;
            let mut end = i + prefix.len();
            while end < bytes.len() && (bytes[end].is_ascii_uppercase() || bytes[end] == b'_' || bytes[end].is_ascii_digit()) {
                end += 1;
            }
            if (end >= bytes.len() || !ident(bytes[end])) && bytes[end - 1] != b'_' {
                out.push(text[start..end].to_owned());
            }
            i = end;
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Every refusal code the engine, the compiler and the client emit is one
/// `snapback4 why` explains — the orientation's promise, tested.
#[test]
fn every_emitted_code_is_explained() {
    let known = codes();
    // The placeholder in `why`'s usage line.
    let not_codes = ["E_CODE"];
    let mut unexplained = BTreeMap::<String, Vec<String>>::new();
    for file in sources() {
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&file).unwrap();
        for word in code_words(&text) {
            if !known.contains(&word.as_str()) && !not_codes.contains(&word.as_str()) {
                unexplained.entry(word).or_default().push(file.strip_prefix(Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../..")).unwrap().display().to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    for (code, files) in &mut unexplained {
        files.sort();
        files.dedup();
        let _ = code;
    }
    assert!(unexplained.is_empty(), "codes `why` cannot explain (add them to guide::CODES):\n{}", unexplained.iter().map(|(code, files)| format!("  {code}: {}", files.join(", "))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n"));
    for code in &known {
        assert!(explain_code(code).is_some_and(|text| text.starts_with(&format!("{code}: "))), "{code}");
    }
    assert!(explain_code("E_NOPE").is_none());
}

}

        .replace("web uses the wasm\ndevice", "web uses the wasm device")
        .replace("web uses the\nwasm device", "web uses the wasm device");

//! Query result paths and nullable reads of private side tables.
use super::*;

pub(super) const VIEWER_KEY: &str = "$lookupViewerKey";
const TARGET_ROW: &str = "$lookupTargetRow";

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#151-evidence-and-decision — compatibility keeps
// fallthrough null; check must name a concrete uncovered source path.
pub(super) fn fallthrough(decl: &ast::ProgramDecl) -> Diagnostic {
    fn path(body: &[S], implicit: bool) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
        let mut route = Vec::new();
        for (at, stmt) in body.iter().enumerate() {
            match stmt {
                S::Return { .. } => return None,
                S::Expr { .. } if implicit && at + 1 == body.len() => return None,
                S::Require { condition: A::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(false), .. }, .. } => return None,
                S::If { then_body, else_body, site, .. } => {
                    let completes = implicit && at + 1 == body.len();
                    let (arm, rest) = if let Some(rest) = path(then_body, completes) { ("true", rest) }
                        else if let Some(rest) = path(else_body, completes) { ("false", rest) }
                        else { return None };
                    route.push(format!("if at {site} is {arm}")); route.extend(rest);
                }
                S::For { site, .. } => route.push(format!("loop at {site} has zero iterations")),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Some(route)
    }
    let route = path(&decl.body, true).unwrap_or_default();
    let route = if route.is_empty() { "entry → end".into() } else { format!("{} → end", route.join(" → ")) };
    Diagnostic::new(&decl.site, "N_QUERY_FALLTHROUGH",
        format!("query {} can finish without a result ({route}); that path returns null", decl.name),
        "return a value on this path: add `return []` for an intentionally empty list, or `return null` for intentional absence; a return inside a possibly empty loop does not cover its zero-iteration path").guide("programs")
}

impl Binder<'_> {
    fn lookup_rule_proved(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        let mut copy = value.clone();
        let mut target = false;
        super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut copy, &mut |node| {
            if matches!(node, A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW) { target = true; }
        });
        if !target { return self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(value, true); }
        match value {
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "or" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) || self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) && self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#152-lookup-contract-and-diagnostics — transport
    // only source advice facts across the helper's captured argument boundary.
    pub(super) fn helper_lookup_points(&self, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A]) -> Vec<ReadExpr> {
        fn closed(value: &A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl]) -> bool {
            let mut value = value.clone();
            let mut safe = true;
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value, &mut |node| match node {
                A::Name { name, .. } if name != "viewer" && name != "now" && !parameters.iter().any(|p| p.name == *name) => safe = false,
                A::Focal { .. } | A::Write { .. } | A::Call { .. } => safe = false,
                _ => {}
            });
            safe
        }
        fn substitute(value: &mut A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl], args: &[A]) {
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(value, &mut |node| {
                if let A::Name { name, .. } = node && let Some(at) = parameters.iter().position(|p| p.name == *name)
                    && let Some(argument) = args.get(at) { *node = argument.clone(); }
            });
        }
        fn collect(catalog: &Catalog, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A], stack: &mut Vec<String>, fuel: &mut usize, reads: &mut Vec<ReadExpr>) {
            if stack.len() >= 32 || stack.contains(&function.name) { return; }
            stack.push(function.name.clone());
            let mut body = match &function.body { ast::FunctionBody::Block(body) => body.clone(), ast::FunctionBody::Expression(value) => vec![S::Return { value: value.clone(), site: value.site().clone() }] };
            super::super::intent_walk::statements(&mut body, &mut |node| {
                if *fuel == 0 { return; } *fuel -= 1;
                match node {
                    A::Read(read) if read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args)) => {
                        let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
                        if let A::Read(read) = value { reads.push(read); }
                    }
                    A::Call { name, args: arguments, .. } if arguments.iter().all(|value| closed(value, &function.args)) => {
                        if let Some(callee) = catalog.functions.get(name) {
                            let mut arguments = arguments.clone();
                            for value in &mut arguments { substitute(value, &function.args, args); }
                            collect(catalog, callee, &arguments, stack, fuel, reads);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            });
            stack.pop();
        }
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation { return Vec::new(); }
        let identity: Vec<_> = function.args.iter().map(|p| A::Name { name: p.name.clone(), site: p.site.clone() }).collect();
        let mut reads = Vec::new();
        collect(self.catalog, function, &identity, &mut Vec::new(), &mut 512, &mut reads);
        reads.into_iter().filter(|read| read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args))).filter(|read| {
            let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
            let A::Read(actual) = value else { return false };
            self.point_guard_safe(&A::Read(actual.clone())) && (self.point_present(&actual) || self.lookup_point_present(&actual) || self.row_independent_read_proved(&actual.table))
        }).collect()
    }
    // This marker suppresses advice only; it cannot authorize a runtime read
    // or enter the binder's authority/presence proof domains.
    pub(super) fn lookup_viewer_key(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        if matches!(value, A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" || self.binding(name)
            .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.contains_key(&vec![VIEWER_KEY.into()]))) { return true; }
        let equal = A::Binary { op: "=".into(), left: Box::new(value.clone()), right: Box::new(A::Name { name: "viewer".into(), site: value.site().clone() }), site: value.site().clone() };
        self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(&equal, true)
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — asserted and same-table reads still need reader authority; blind writes do not pass here.
    pub(super) fn optional_lookup_note(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, point: &Read) {
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation || self.point_present(read) || self.lookup_point_present(read)
            || self.row_independent_read_proved(&read.table) { return; }
        let table = &self.schema.tables[&read.table];
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() || self.schema.maintain_for(&read.table).is_some() { return; }
        let index = &table.indexes[&point.index];
        let pinned = index.components.iter().zip(&point.key).filter_map(|(part, value)| part.column().map(|name| (name, value))).collect();
        if snapback4_core::engine::rules::prefix_visibility(&read.table, table, &table.rules.read, &pinned).decided_true { return; }
        if let Some(rule) = self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read) {
            let named = read.keys.iter().all(|key| key.column.is_some());
            let keys: BTreeMap<_, _> = read.keys.iter().enumerate().filter_map(|(at, key)|
                Some((if named { key.column.clone()? } else { index.components.get(at)?.column()?.clone() },
                    if self.lookup_viewer_key(&key.value) { A::Name { name: "viewer".into(), site: key.site.clone() } } else { key.value.clone() }))).collect();
            let mut condition = rule.value.clone();
            // Rule constants and target fields occupy their own namespaces.
            // Freeze/seal them before injecting lexical caller key expressions.
            maintain_types::normalize_rule_constants(&mut condition);
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut condition, &mut |value| {
                if let A::Member { base, .. } = value && let A::Focal { site } = base.as_ref() {
                    **base = A::Name { name: TARGET_ROW.into(), site: site.clone() };
                }
            });
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut condition, &mut |value| {
                if let A::Member { base, name, .. } = value && matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW)
                    && let Some(key) = keys.get(name) { *value = key.clone(); }
            });
            if self.lookup_rule_proved(&condition) { return; }
        }
        let rule = table.through.as_ref().map_or_else(|| format!("read <- {}", table.rules.read.quarry()), |through| format!("read through .{}", through.reference));
        let location = self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read)
            .map(|rule| rule.site.to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|| self.catalog.tables[&read.table].decl.site.to_string());
        if self.notes.iter().any(|note| note.code == "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED" && note.site == read.site) { return; }
        self.notes.push(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "N_LOOKUP_FILTERED",
            format!("mutation {}: lookup of {} uses `{rule}` ({location}); its key and preceding guards do not prove read authority. A hidden, expired or missing row returns null; `! else CODE` refuses with that authored code for all three. A later field/default or require may report a different business condition", self.name, read.table),
            "review whether these callers should read this data; use a deliberately readable projection containing only the needed fields, or keep null as intentional absence. An id and a later write rule do not grant read authority; do not widen private rows just to read one field").guide("rules"));
    }
}

# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.

import { requireOptionalNativeModule } from "expo-modules-core";
import { createWitness, type Witness, type WitnessContainer } from "./witness-core";
export type { Witness } from "./witness-core";

import { witnessRuntime } from "./witness-runtime";

let instance: Witness | null | undefined;
/** Null on ordinary launches and outside an iOS simulator driven by `snapback4 witness ios`. */
export function witness(): Witness | null {
  if (instance === undefined) {
    const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
    instance = container?.witnessLaunch && JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch).smoke === true ? null : createWitness(container, witnessRuntime());
  }
  return instance;
}

/** The starter may use normal guest sign-in during prime; never on ordinary launches. */
export function smokeSegment(): "prime" | "offline" | "restart" | null {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return null;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && ["prime", "offline", "restart"].includes(config.segment) ? config.segment : null;
}

/** Simulator smoke uses its owned loopback backend; ordinary launches keep the app URL. */
export function smokeOrigin(fallback: string): string {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return fallback;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && /^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]+$/.test(config.origin) ? config.origin : fallback;
}

/** Disposable account supplied only by the owned prime smoke launch. */
export function smokeAccount(): { email: string; password: string } | null {
  const container = requireOptionalNativeModule<WitnessContainer>("Snapback4");
  if (!container?.witnessLaunch) return null;
  const config = JSON.parse(container.witnessLaunch);
  return config.smoke === true && config.segment === "prime" && typeof config.smokeAccount?.email === "string" && typeof config.smokeAccount?.password === "string" ? config.smokeAccount : null;
}
